73e12fa9c5244f04: NEW YORK: Ben Shelton believes his newly acquired problem-solving skills can carry him to a maiden Grand Slam title when he faces Alexander Zverev in the final of the US Open on Sunday.
The big-serving 23-year-old powered into the first major championship final of his career on Friday after muscling his way past close friend Frances Tiafoe in an all-American semi-final.
The eighth-seeded Shelton was in irresistible form as he stormed to a 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 victory in front of a raucous home crowd at the Arthur Ashe Stadium.
It was another impressive milestone on Shelton's journey through this year's tournament, which included an epic five-set victory in the quarter-finals over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz.
Shelton, who blasted 20 aces in Friday's semi-final win, said his success at Flushing Meadows this year has been based on his ability to align brain with brawn.
"I think that problem-solving has been the name of the game here," said Shelton, who had never beaten Alcaraz in three previous meetings before his last-eight triumph over the Spanish star.
"It's been a lot of uphill battle, so I think that I'm fully ready for the challenge to problem-solve," Shelton said.

"I feel that I'm a different player. I feel like I have so many more tools. I feel like I know my identity, am comfortable in my own skin, and I know what it takes for me to be playing top-level tennis.
"I'm looking forward to the challenge, being able to problem-solve on Sunday. I know what I'm up against, and I'm also the most confident I've ever been in my game.

"For me, this whole tournament now at this point has been uncharted territory. I'm in positions I've never been in before. I've beaten guys that I have never beaten before. I'm just excited to put it all out on the line."
Shelton is now one win away from becoming the first American man to win a Grand Slam title in 23 years. The last player to lift a major was Andy Roddick at the 2003 US Open.
He is adamant he will not be burdened by the weight of history in Sunday's final.
"I think that I handle these big situations in my career pretty well," Shelton said. "I feel that confidence and belief take over.

"The nerves are always there. It's something that you got to kind of lean into. The nerves are as much there in the first round for me as in the semi-finals, and I'm sure that the finals will be the same.

"It's something you've got to be able to overcome, but for me I'm having fun, you know? This is an enjoyable moment for me and knowing that I can leave it all out there on the court and push myself to the absolute limit is an exciting, exciting thought." - AFP
da5b9d06317b8fbc: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is ready to contest all 28 seats in the upcoming Melaka election if necessary.

Acting Melaka PKR chief Adam Adli Abd Halim said this when asked about the coalition's preparedness for the polls amid reports of planned talks between PH and Barisan Nasional, which rules the state with a two-thirds majority.
"We must always be prepared because whether to negotiate or not is a choice, and every party has the right to decide.
"Contesting all seats will not be an issue for us, as we have done so before," he said on the sidelines of the Kampung Angkat Madani programme in Kampung Sungai Putat.
Previously, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said BN would only begin negotiations after the dissolution of the Melaka State Assembly, which he hinted would happen soon.
Adam Adli said Melaka PH wanted the upcoming polls to be a healthy contest and not a source of division.
"Elections should not affect harmony in the state," he said.
d2b1cdeb5e8c34b6: HONG KONG: Veteran Hong Kong actor Simon Lui, celebrated for his iconic roles in horror movies, has died from stomach cancer. He was 62.
​Hong Kong media reported on Sept 11 that his wife, Chinese streaming host Ma Li, confirmed he passed away peacefully on Sept 7 in Guangzhou, China, following a relapse of his condition a year ago.
The family has requested a private funeral service.
​Affectionately dubbed the "King of Ghosts" by fans and industry peers, Lui launched his entertainment career after graduating from TVB's acting course in 1988.
He shot to fame throughout the 1990s as a mainstay of Hong Kong's supernatural genre, starring in numerous horror features and hosting popular paranormal television broadcasts.
​His most notable breakthrough arrived with the 1997 comedy-horror hit Troublesome Night.
The film launched a successful 20-part franchise, with Lui featuring prominently in 13 of the installments.
He married Ma Li, who is 21 years younger, in 2012 and they have a son.
​In recent years, Lui maintained a low profile, residing in Guangzhou with his family.
0f3077ba107ff89d: KUCHING, Sept 12 — Sarawak is pushing for regulatory powers under the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 (Act 586) to be decentralised to the state Health Department (JKNS), said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian.
He said the matter was among three key areas of Sarawak’s health autonomy that he raised on Friday’s Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting in Kota Kinabalu.
“The one that impacts most is the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 (Act 586),” he shared in his Facebook post.

He said the regulatory function should be decentralised to JKNS from the Ministry of Health (MOH), in line with the MOH White Paper and provisions under the Federal Constitution allowing such delegation of power.
Dr Sim also called for urgent action to address Sarawak’s shortage of health personnel, with 5,654 vacant posts currently under JKNS.
He said the vacancies accounted for 18 per cent of the state health workforce and staff were not only overworked but also facing burnout.
For the medium term, he proposed the creation of 11,000 posts across various categories to meet MOH staffing norms following an audit of seven Sarawak hospitals last year.
“There is no reason for Sarawak to be sub-standard in manpower,” he said.
On infrastructure, Dr Sim said Sarawak needed RM310 million to upgrade dilapidated Klinik Kesihatan (KK) facilities and RM8.45 billion for their redevelopment.
He said 160 of the state’s 271 KKs, or 66 per cent, were classified as dilapidated.
“There is no reason why Sarawak having more KK daif compared to the rest of Malaysia,” he said.
Dr Sim said health was among the more complex MA63 matters, involving 41 laws.

He said while some MA63 issues had been resolved, the remaining negotiations would be tougher as some involved constitutional amendments requiring approval at Cabinet and Parliament level and, in certain cases, the Conference of Rulers.
He said the negotiations must take into account the spirit of MA63, as well as the Cobbold Commission and Inter-Governmental Committee reports.
“MA63 is a journey. We shall move forward with courage, wisdom and the spirit of our founding fathers,” he said. — The Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: Daif in Malay, used in the quote above by Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Dr Sim Kui Hian, means dilapidated.
be46090fd4565dd9: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are still hunting for the armed robbers who broke into a condominium unit on Jalan Ampang on Monday and made off with RM2.9 million in cash and valuables.
Wangsa Maju police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said there were no new developments at the moment.
"The investigation is ongoing, so give us some time to work," he said when contacted.
It was reported earlier that the 28-year-old victim, a Chinese national, suffered losses amounting to RM2.9 million after a group of knife-wielding men broke into his home on Monday afternoon.
The victim lodged a police report the same evening.
Police are also probing the possibility of an inside job, given the tight security at the condominium. Statements have been taken from 12 witnesses.
The case is being investigated under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery and gang robbery with a deadly weapon.
The offences are punishable by a maximum 20-year jail term and caning.
32dc7099a58a7ac3: PARIS, Sept 12 — Adrien Thomasson scored the only goal of the game as Rennes went provisionally top of Ligue 1 on Friday with a 1-0 win over Marseille, who slumped to a third successive defeat.
Thomasson converted from close range early in the second half in Brittany after Mousa Al-Tamari had nodded the ball back across goal, as Rennes claimed a third consecutive win.

The goal-scorer later saw another effort come back off the crossbar but Rennes held on to move onto 10 points, one point above Monaco. The principality club have won all of their three matches so far and can reclaim first place when they go to Strasbourg on Saturday.
Marseille created plenty of their own chances but it looks like their inability to make any new signings in the summer transfer window may come back to haunt them.

Financially hamstrung after failing to qualify for this season’s Champions League, Marseille sold several key players including top scorer Mason Greenwood and Dutch midfielder Quinten Timber, and did not replace them.

They appointed a new coach in Bruno Genesio from Lille, but he is being forced to field a side which includes players who were on the fringes of the team last season and others who have returned from spells away on loan.

They beat Strasbourg 4-0 on the opening night of the campaign but have not picked up a point since, and their next two matches are away to Besiktas in the Europa League and at home to Paris Saint-Germain.
Reigning champions PSG have not yet won a Ligue 1 game this season before they go to Brest on Sunday.
Paris FC and Lyon, who have both started the campaign strongly, face each other in the capital on Saturday. — AFP
0f568f5186bd87e9: KUALA LUMPUR: The FA of Malaysia (FAM) must stop wasting millions of ringgit on penalties and channel those funds into grassroots development instead, says Datuk Seri Shahril Mokhtar, who will contest for the association's president post on Sept 17.
FAM's audited financial statements for the year ended Dec 31, 2025 showed RM2.58 million spent under the penalty category.
Shahril, who is Selangor FA deputy president, said the amount was enough to provide a basic RM100,000 grant to each affiliate member for grassroots programmes.
"This shows that FAM's challenge is not merely about finding funds, but how existing funds are managed," he said in a statement.
He said a transparent FAM could avoid costs from governance failures and redirect resources towards development at the affiliate level.
Shahril proposed that the national body work closely with affiliate members through structured grants with clear conditions to ensure proper use of the funds.

"I believe FAM needs to work closely with all affiliate members through structured grants, ensuring that every ringgit reaches sports development, rather than covering the cost of avoidable mistakes," he said.
Shahril said financial transparency, professionalism, and accountability form part of his "Berani Ubah" agenda.
Shahril will contesnt against Malaysian Football League president Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan for the top post in the FAM election on Sept 17.
3628df5037dbed26: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's disaster assistance and rescue team (SMART) is expected to return home today or tomorrow from Nepal after taking part in the search for 55 Malaysians still missing following the floods and landslides in the country.
Foreign minister Mohamad Hasan stressed that Nepali authorities had no plans to end the search and rescue operations as about 5,000 people remained unaccounted for.

“The team will return to Malaysia. But they will hand over all the drones brought from here to the Nepali rescue teams for their use,” he told reporters during a visit to the media centre at the 2026 Umno general assembly here today.
The 11 SMART personnel left for Nepal last Saturday, with 12.4 tonnes of search and rescue equipment, on a mission that was originally expected to last 10 days.
The Aug 26 floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border have killed hundreds of people and left thousands more missing, according to Nepali and Chinese authorities.
Mohamad said there had been no new developments or trace of the missing Malaysians.
He said the last known locations of their mobile phones were in areas that were badly affected by the disaster.
Mohamad said the Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu was in discussions with Nepal’s foreign and law ministries to establish the status of the missing Malaysians.
He said this is because Nepali law stipulated that a death certificate for a missing person could only be issued after three years, compared with seven years in Malaysia.
“If possible, we want to establish a legal mechanism so that matters such as insurance and other claims can be dealt with immediately," he said.

Mohamad said Malaysia was also seeking Nepal’s cooperation to allow DNA samples from bodies recovered to be sent to Kuala Lumpur for matching against samples from the families of the missing Malaysians.
He said Nepal faced a shortage of facilities and equipment to conduct DNA matching.
3a36bdd6d5324fc1: JAKARTA, Sept 12 — A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck near Jakarta’s Thousand Islands (Kepulauan Seribu) early Saturday, with tremors felt in the Indonesian capital and across parts of Java and Sumatra.

Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) Earthquake and Tsunami Director Dr Wijayanto said the earthquake struck at 4.23am local time, with the magnitude revised from an initial 5.9 following further analysis.
He said its epicentre was in the Java Sea, 69 kilometres north-east of Jakarta’s Thousand Islands, at a depth of 368 kilometres.

“Taking into account the location of the epicentre and the depth of its hypocentre, the earthquake was a deep earthquake caused by intraslab activity,” he said in a statement, adding that tsunami modelling showed no tsunami threat.

The earthquake came less than 10 hours after a magnitude 6.0 quake struck the Banda Sea in eastern Indonesia at 6.56pm on Friday at a depth of 148 kilometres, with its epicentre 162 kilometres northeast of South-west Maluku and tremors felt across parts of Maluku.

Wijayanto said the strongest tremors from Saturday’s earthquake were reported in parts of Banten and West Java, as well as Tanggamus in southern Sumatra, where the shaking was perceptible by people indoors and could cause windows and doors to rattle.

He said the tremors were also clearly felt indoors in Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok and several other areas, while weaker shaking was reported as far away as Yogyakarta and Malang in Java, and Padang and the Mentawai Islands in western Sumatra.

Some of strongest tremors were reportedly felt in Pandeglang in Banten, which lies along the Sunda Strait near the Anak Krakatau volcano which experienced renewed eruptive activity last week. However, Wijayanto said, Saturday’s earthquake was tectonic in origin, with BMKG reporting no aftershocks as of 5am.
Meanwhile, KAI Commuter said in a social media post that Commuter Line services were suspended following the earthquake to allow comprehensive inspections of railway tracks.
It said the Bogor, Cikarang, Rangkasbitung, and Tanjung Priok lines resumed services after inspections were completed at 5.26am, followed by the Tangerang line at 5.45am. — Bernama
d96c38c8eb1b429c: PHOENIX: Arizona has sued L'Oreal SA and its US subsidiary, alleging the cosmetics company hid evidence that its hair relaxer products could cause cancer in women, as it faces thousands of similar lawsuits from users and their families.

Arizona Attorney General Kristin Mayes, a Democrat, filed the lawsuit late Thursday in state court, making Arizona the first state to sue over alleged cancer risks linked to hair relaxers. The lawsuit accuses L'Oreal of violating state consumer protection laws by marketing the products without warning consumers about the alleged risks of ovarian and uterine cancers.
The state is seeking penalties and damages, as well as a court order forcing L’Oreal to stop selling the products unless it warns of the cancer risk.

The lawsuit comes as the company faces more than 12,000 similar lawsuits filed by women or their families that have been consolidated in a Chicago federal court as part of a multidistrict litigation proceeding, a procedure designed to more efficiently manage lawsuits filed in multiple jurisdictions.
A spokesman for L’Oreal USA said the company is confident in the safety of its products and believes the claims are without legal or scientific merit.
The products, which have been marketed under the names Dark and Lovely, Optimum and other brands, promise to permanently straighten textured hair.

The first lawsuits hit the docket after the 2022 release of a study done by the National Institutes of Health that found women who used the products several times a year were more than twice as likely to develop uterine cancer.
L'Oreal's spokesman said Friday the study made no finding of a causal connection between the use of those products and any conditions alleged by the plaintiffs.
The lawsuits seek damages to compensate the women for their pain and suffering and economic damages for medical bills and the cost of the products, among other things.
The lawsuits name L’Oreal, as well as Revlon and other makers of the products. Revlon has also denied a connection between cancer and the products.
The multidistrict litigation continues to move forward, court records show, and trials could begin next year.
36934048bad9ba30: KUALA LUMPUR: It is common for political parties to seek a fresh mandate from voters after a government had been in power for three years, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
Speaking on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today, he said the current government had now been in power for more than three years.
"Now it has been more than three years. Typically, the mood for holding an election comes after three years.
"Whether it should be held or not is up to them.
"Political parties will always want to seek a fresh mandate from the people," he said.
Mohamad said Umno, as one of the political parties with a stake in the country's political landscape, also wanted to secure a fresh mandate from its supporters and voters.
Yesterday, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi declared an all-out war against the party's political rivals when he reiterated his call for an early 16th General Election (GE16).
He said the call reflected the wishes of the people rather than a demand or hope from the party.

Meanwhile, on Kedah Umno information chief Datuk Shaiful Hazizy Zainol Abidin's remark that the state chapter would begin political cooperation talks with Pas, but not Perikatan Nasional (PN), Mohamad said any discussions at the state level should be brought to the attention of the party headquarters.
"Let them hold whatever discussions they want at the state level. Whatever discussions they have, they need to bring them to the attention of the headquarters.
"When the time comes, the top leadership will review all the negotiations and discussions that have taken place because, as I mentioned, there is no one-size-fits-all approach.
"We want to diversify because the political situation in the country is no longer uniform. So, we cannot use one formula that can be applied to every state," he said.

c772640794000946: PETALING JAYA: Jabatan Penjara nafi wujudn layanan berbeza berhubung pelepasan bekas menteri pembangunan infrastruktur Sabah, Peter Anthony, di bawah program Pelepasan Banduan Secara Berlesen (PBSL).
Jabatan itu dalam kenyataan, memaklumkan Anthony hanya dipertimbangkan untuk parol selepas memenuhi tempoh kelayakan ditetapkan serta menjalani proses saringan dan penilaian.

Menurut kenyataan itu, prospek perlu terlebih dulu menjalani sekurang-kurangnya satu pertiga daripada tempoh hukuman untuk dipertimbangkan, namun pemenuhan tempoh tersebut tidak memberikan kelayakan automatik untu prospek diberikan PBSL.
"PBSL bukan penghapusan, pemendekan atau pengurangan hukuman yang telah dijatuhkan oleh mahkamah.

"Prospek yang diberikan PBSL masih menjalani baki tempoh hukuman, namun pelaksanaannya diteruskan dalam komuniti tertakluk kepada syarat, peraturan, pengawasan dan pemantauan Jabatan Penjara," katanya.
Peter disabitkan pada 2022 kerana memalsukan surat daripada pejabat Timbalan Naib Canselor Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) 11 tahun lalu, berhubung kontrak penyelenggaraan dan perkhidmatan.

Beliau diperintah mula menjalani hukuman penjara tiga tahun pada tahun lalu susulan penolakan rayuan terakhirnya untuk membatalkan sabitan itu, pada 4 Mac 2025. Beliau kemudiannya dilepaskan secara parol pada Mac lalu.
Jabatan Penjara berkata, keputusan parol dibuat oleh satu jawatankuasa dipengerusikan komisioner jeneral penjara serta dianggotai pegawai kanan dan wakil agensi berkaitan.

Katanya, pelaksanaan PBSL berteraskan prinsip pemulihan dalam komuniti yang mengimbangi kepentingan keselamatan awam, pemulihan individu, pengawasan serta persediaan untuk reintegrasi ke dalam keluarga dan masyarakat.

"PBSL dilaksanakan kepada prospek yang layak tanpa mengira latar belakang, kedudukan, status atau pengaruh seseorang. Status individu bukan kriteria yang memberikan kelebihan atau pengecualian daripada proses kelayakan dan penilaian yang ditetapkan."
Jabatan itu menegaskan dakwaan bahawa pelepasan melalui PBSL diberikan atas layanan berbeza atau dwistandard adalah tidak tepat.

"Setiap pertimbangan dibuat berdasarkan kelayakan, penilaian dan proses yang ditetapkan, manakala prospek yang diberikan PBSL kekal tertakluk kepada pengawasan sehingga selesai menjalani baki tempoh hukumannya.

Sebelum ini, Presiden MCA, Wee Ka Siong, mempersoalkan mengapa tiada sebarang bantahan daripada Pakatan Harapan apabila Peter dilepaskan secara parol. Beliau membandingkan situasi ini dengan seruan gabungan itu agar mereka disabitkan kesalahan rasuah atau penyalahgunaan kuasa terutamanya kes berprofil tinggi menjalani hukuman penjara sepenuhnya.
Isu ini timbul di tengah-tengah permohonan pengampunan bekas perdana menteri, Najib Razak, berhubung sabitan kes yang dikaitkan dengan skandal 1MDB.
fbe7f73a9b5ebbd1: SINGAPORE, Sept 12 — Fitness and yoga chains True Fitness and True Yoga are shutting down in Singapore after their Hong Kong parent company said the businesses could no longer continue because of their liabilities.

The Straits Times reported that Kontafarma China Holdings announced on September 10 that the directors of True Fitness and True Yoga had resolved to wind up the businesses, citing mounting liabilities and intense market competition.

Singapore’s consumer rights watchdog Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) said members of the two chains had reported more than S$609,000 (RM1.96 million) in losses from unused memberships, packages and services.
CASE president Melvin Yong said in a Facebook post on September 11 that the agency had received 241 complaints by 6pm, up from 28 complaints earlier that day.

“CASE has reached out to the provisional liquidator and will continue to seek clarification on the arrangements for affected consumers, including information required for consumers to lodge their claims,” he said.
Two employees told ST they were informed of the sudden closure by email at about 10.30pm on September 10, roughly an hour before the outlets were due to shut.
The email from the company’s human resources department said: “all outlets will be closed effective immediately and are not to be opened tomorrow (September 11)”.

The True Singapore Group, which operates True Fitness, True Yoga, TFX and Yoga Edition, said all outlets under the brands would close as part of the winding-up process, with the group reporting a loss of HK$34.3 million on revenue of HK$181.2 million in 2025.

Its unaudited accounts for the eight months to August 31 this year showed revenue of HK$118.4 million and a loss of HK$19.1 million, while liabilities stood at HK$633.8 million against assets of HK$204.5 million, leaving net liabilities of HK$429.3 million.

Kontafarma said the group was facing unprecedented challenges from competition posed by boutique gyms, fitness apps and online coaching, while more residential developments were offering gym facilities to residents.

“While the best endeavours have been made to control costs and optimise operational efficiency of the fitness business in Singapore, the fitness business has found it extremely difficult to continue amid the fiercely challenging market,” it said.

Insolvency practitioners Goh Wee Teck and Lin Yueh Hung of RSM SG Corporate Advisory have been appointed provisional liquidators, while creditors’ voluntary winding-up proposals for True Fitness and True Yoga will be considered at extraordinary general meetings on October 7.

As at September 11, the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority’s BizFile records showed both companies as being in liquidation, while several outlets had been shuttered with liquidation or repossession notices posted at their entrances.

ST reported that a member who had paid S$79 for a monthly gym membership on September 9, just a day before the closure announcement, said she was shocked by the sudden shutdown, while the company’s former employees were also seeking clarity over outstanding September salaries.
30b13f668161415d: KUALA LUMPUR: What an embarrassment. How much lower can Malaysian hockey go?
While fans expected Malaysia to steamroll Bangladesh in their women's Junior Asia Cup classification match today and qualify for the Junior World Cup (JWC), the opposite happened.
Bangladesh stunned the Young Tigresses 2-1 in Inner Mongolia, China, to finish fifth and claim the final ticket to the JWC.
The South Asian side took a two-goal lead through Sharika Rimon in the 31st minute and Kona Akter in the 50th before Irdina Humaira Jeffrey pulled one back for Malaysia in the 59th.
Malaysia ended their campaign in China without a win, losing all six matches, scoring just three goals and conceding 26.
It is certainly embarrassing, considering Malaysia qualified for last year's women's JWC in Chile on merit.

The Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) must take responsibility for this failure, which raises serious questions about the effectiveness of the country's grassroots programmes in producing quality players.
National coach Nasihin Nubli said his players wasted too many opportunities against Bangladesh.
"They tried, but their efforts were not good enough. However, some of the umpire decisions also played a part in our defeat.
"These players are young, with an average age of 16, and they are still lacking physical strength, which was obvious when they attended a recent national training camp.
"The states should build their players. We will continue to train for upcoming tournaments," said Nasihin.
d0dd52f163521bf2: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim began Saturday with his first bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, as Malaysia seeks to deepen economic ties with Iran while navigating mounting geopolitical and sanctions-related risks.

Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, and other Malaysian delegates are also at the meeting, held at The Oberoi Hotel here.
The talks are expected to focus on bilateral relations, particularly opportunities to expand trade, investment and economic cooperation between the two countries.

Anwar had said earlier this year that Malaysia would maintain its trade and diplomatic relations with Iran despite United States President Donald Trump's announcement of a 25 per cent tariff on goods from countries doing business with Teheran.
He said Malaysia's relationship with Iran remained intact and would continue to be guided by prudence, national interest and respect for the sovereignty of other nations.

Anwar also stressed that Malaysia would exercise wisdom in managing its international relations, ensuring that the country neither appeared weak nor took actions that could jeopardise its national interests.

Malaysia-Iran bilateral trade stood at RM2.45 billion in 2025, the bulk of which were exports at RM2.17 billion. Exports largely comprised palm oil, while imports included Iranian oil and gas products.

The meeting comes as Malaysia seeks to leverage its BRICS membership to broaden economic engagement with emerging markets, with Iran's membership providing another avenue for trade, investment and economic cooperation.
The two countries have previously identified areas for closer cooperation including trade, investment, education, healthcare and research.
However, the engagement comes against a backdrop of heightened tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel, alongside growing scrutiny of Iranian energy exports and maritime activities.

For Malaysia, this creates a delicate balancing act between expanding legitimate economic ties with Iran and shielding Malaysian companies, financial institutions and maritime operators from potential sanctions and trade-related repercussions.

At 10.30am local time, Anwar is scheduled to meet his Indian counterpart and summit host Narendra Modi, before holding a third bilateral meeting later in the day with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
He is also scheduled to hold a pull-aside meeting with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

Anwar will then hold a series of one-on-one meetings with Indian business leaders, including Adani Group, which has established major interests in transport, logistics, energy and large-scale infrastructure development in India.

Other meetings are scheduled with Segula Technologies India Pvt Ltd, a global engineering group; AWL Agri Business Ltd, one of India's major food and fast-moving consumer goods companies; and Motherson Group, a global design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly and logistics specialist.
Anwar will later attend a gala dinner for leaders of BRICS member, partner and outreach countries at Bharat Mandapam, the exhibition and convention centre where the summit is being held.
acb76201df83845d: SINGAPORE, Sept 12 — Home-grown bakery Baker’s Brew Studio, which rebranded as BB Atelier last year, has gone into liquidation after the company was found unable to continue its business due to its liabilities.

According to AsiaOne, the company resolved at a creditors’ meeting on Aug 31 to enter creditors’ voluntary liquidation, with Goh Wee Teck and Lin Yueh Hung appointed as liquidators under a resolution dated September 8.
The bakery is also facing several civil proceedings, including a negligence suit brought by PSGourmet, the company behind restaurant chain PS.Cafe, which was heard at the State Courts on Sept 1.
Baker’s Brew Studio is also the defendant in two other ongoing civil cases.
Business records list founder and director Beh Huat Jin and Toh Capital as shareholders of the company, which was incorporated in November 2014.

Baker’s Brew started as a baking studio in Sembawang in February 2015 before opening a second outlet in Upper Thomson the following year and a studio-cafe at Paragon in 2017, according to a 2019 post on recruitment platform Wantedly.
The bakery later expanded to Great World City, but all four outlets are now listed as permanently closed on Google, despite having ratings of between 4.7 and 4.8 stars from more than 3,000 reviews.

The company announced in November 2025 that it was changing its name from Baker’s Brew to BB Atelier, while Manila-based creative boutique Studio After Six, which worked on the rebranding, posted about the change on Instagram in July this year.

However, the bakery’s Facebook and Instagram accounts have been inactive since May, while its Shopee store indicates that the seller was last active about 15 weeks ago and is currently marked as being “on vacation”.
The Shopee store still lists about 40 food products, including a mao shan wang durian coconut origami cake, and has about 3,800 followers with an average rating of 4.8 stars.

The website linked to the bakery’s social media accounts is also no longer accessible, while a comment on one of its Instagram posts alleged that the company owed a supplier about S$29,000 (RM93,184), although the claim has not been independently verified.
AsiaOne reported that it had contacted the account behind the comment and Baker’s Brew Studio for comment.
c166fa3df27803f9: CORPORATE social responsibility (CSR) has become a common practice among major corporations, reflecting a commitment to supporting communities rather than focusing solely on profits.

While many companies publicise their CSR initiatives to raise awareness about social issues, such campaigns often place greater emphasis on corporate achievements than on the communities that have endured hardship before receiving assistance.
For Allianz Malaysia Berhad, however, CSR is driven by a different philosophy.
"Some companies like us undertake CSR simply because it is the right thing to do," Allianz Malaysia chairman Zakri Mohd Khir told Business Times.
He said the company's CSR focus has remained unchanged over the past 25 years, creating greater equality for underserved communities through its CSR arm.
"As communities face change and disruption, we focus on reducing gaps and creating more equitable opportunities.
MAKING MOBILITY ACCESSIBLE

Zakri recalled one of Allianz Malaysia's earliest CSR projects in 2006, when it partnered with Persatuan Mobiliti Selangor dan Kuala Lumpur (Mobiliti to provide door-to-door transport services for wheelchair users in the Klang Valley.
The initiative introduced specially modified vans fitted with hydraulic lifts and wheelchair restraint systems, allowing passengers to travel safely for a minimal fee.
Allianz Malaysia funded the vans' operating costs, enabling Mobiliti to continue its impactful work towards the people with disabilities (PWD) community.
"Mobiliti existed long before e-hailing services arrived in Malaysia. We were already helping a small community by improving mobility for PWD around Kuala Lumpur.

The idea of providing a taxi-like service using purpose-built vans came from Mobiliti. The association approached us, and we felt it was an excellent initiative, so we funded the specially equipped vehicles, Zakri said.
REACHING REMOTE COMMUNITIES
As Allianz Malaysia celebrates its 25 years in the country this year, the company is grateful for the trust and support that has enabled its growth.
Over the years, the company has undertaken numerous CSR initiatives covering education, support for PWDs and disaster relief.
"Being a responsible corporate citizen means every successful business has a responsibility to invest in the people and communities that have contributed to its success," Zakri added.
Among the projects that left the greatest impression on Zakri was Allianz Malaysia's emergency humanitarian mission during the devastating floods in Kelantan in December 2014.

Several Orang Asli settlements in Gua Musang were completely cut off after heavy rainfall triggered landslides caused by extensive land clearing and logging, preventing rescue teams from delivering food and essentials.
"We received information that seven villages in the Gua Musang highlands had been completely isolated. They had no food for almost two weeks and no assistance.
"We immediately chartered helicopters, delivered food through airdrops and sent medical teams into the area to provide assistance.
"On socio-economic improvement, we are also partnering with Yayasan Kajian Pembangunan Masyarakat to support organic farming and agroforestry among Orang Asli communities in Pekan, Pahang.
"The programme has improved food security and helped families increase their incomes.

"Today, we are building on that progress through collective farming, better infrastructure, skills development and stronger market access to support sustainable livelihoods and long-term community growth."
INVESTING IN CHILDREN'S FUTURE
Beyond disaster relief, Allianz Malaysia has also invested in long-term education initiatives.
On Pulau Tuba, a fishing island in Langkawi, Kedah, the company found many children struggling because of limited educational support.

"We wanted to make a real difference by helping children catch up (on education). We found out that a concerning number of students on the island had dropped out of school post-pandemic while many were left unmotivated," Zakri said.

Through its flagship environmental and education initiative, Allianz Eco Quest (AEQ), the company combines environmental education, gamified learning, shared reading programmes and performance arts to strengthen literacy and teamwork.
Allianz Malaysia has been running community empowerment programmes on Pulau Tuba since 2019, initially focusing on primary schoolchildren.
Between this year and 2028, AEQ will expand to secondary schools with a stronger emphasis on capacity building for youth.
CREATING HOPE THROUGH EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES
Zakri said Allianz Malaysia remains committed to projects that restore hope to communities often overlooked by society.
"There must be some form of equalisation. We believe in making a difference, one initiative at a time.
"At the end of the day, if we can change even one person's life, then every ringgit and every effort we have invested is worthwhile.

"We cast our net as widely as possible through different projects. Hopefully, some will create lasting change. Even if one or two people go on to build a better future, I would consider that a great success," he added.

bc889a1d68802015: KUALA LUMPUR: Terengganu Umno is preparing to recapture the state from Pas at the next election as the party rebuilds its machinery and support across Terengganu.

Former menteri besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Razif Abdul Rahman said Terengganu Umno was preparing to contest on its own, although the state leadership would abide by any decision by the party's national leadership on political cooperation.
"We are preparing on the basis of going solo. If we need to go solo, we go solo. If we need to negotiate, we negotiate.
"If we need an understanding, we have an understanding," he told reporters after debating the Umno president's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Razif, who is also Kuala Nerus Umno chief, said Terengganu Umno was confident it could make a comeback despite its poor showing in the previous state election, when Pas swept all 32 state seats.
"Do not think that what happened in Terengganu, with 32-0, means Umno in Terengganu has disappeared. It has not. I believe Umno has started to rise," he said.

Razif said Terengganu voters were known for changing their political preferences, pointing to the 1999 election when Umno was reduced to four state seats before making a comeback and taking 28 seats in 2004.
"If we managed to turn it around before, from four seats to 28, there is no reason to think it cannot happen again," he said.
He said there were also signs that voters were becoming more willing to compare the performance of the state government with previous administrations.
Razif said the growing focus on "performance politics" could create opportunities for Umno as voters assessed issues affecting their daily lives.
He cited concerns including education, water tariffs, taxes and the distribution of assistance, saying voters had begun questioning some policies implemented by the current administration.
He said strong turnout at Umno-led programmes and events in Terengganu also suggested that public support for the party was recovering.
Razif said the younger generation would be crucial to Umno's efforts to regain the state, adding that the party must offer concrete solutions rather than rely on nostalgia.
He said Umno's approach needed to focus on employment, the economy, agriculture and fisheries, as well as education and skills, to convince younger voters of what the party could deliver.
He also said Umno's preparations for Terengganu were being carried out without formal negotiations with Pas at this stage, as the next state election was still more than two years away.
"The priority now is Melaka and perhaps other states. For Terengganu, we have more than two years," he said.
However, Razif said Terengganu Umno would remain open to political discussions and ultimately accept any decision made by Zahid and the party's top leadership.

a78e98a2c6b60d10: PETALING JAYA: The prisons department has denied allegations of double standards over the release of former Sabah infrastructure minister Peter Anthony under the Licensed Prisoner Release Programme.
The department said Anthony was considered for parole only after having met the stipulated eligibility period and undergone the required screening and assessment process.
A prisoner must have served at least one-third of their sentence to be considered for parole, but meeting the threshold does not automatically qualify them for release, it said.
"His release via parole does not mean the remainder of the sentence handed down by the court has been set aside.
"He continues to serve the remaining sentence term in the community and remains subject to the stipulated conditions, regulations and monitoring throughout that period," it said in a statement today.
Peter was convicted in 2022 of forging a letter from the office of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) deputy vice-chancellor 11 years ago in connection with a maintenance and service contract.

He was ordered to begin serving his three-year jail term last year following the dismissal of his final appeal to have his conviction overturned on March 4, 2025. He was released on parole in March this year.
The prisons department said parole decisions were made by a committee chaired by the commissioner-general of prisons and comprising senior officers and representatives of relevant agencies.

It said assessments took into account several factors, including a prisoner’s good behaviour, rehabilitation progress, participation in rehabilitation programmes, readiness to return to the community, family support and employment opportunities.

"Parole is implemented for eligible prospects regardless of background, position, status or influence. Individual status is not a criterion that confers advantage or exemption from the stipulated eligibility and assessment process," it said.
The department said the programme was part of its community rehabilitation efforts and was intended to balance public safety, rehabilitation, supervision and reintegration into society.
“Therefore, allegations that release through parole is granted based on preferential treatment or double standards are inaccurate,” it said.

MCA president Wee Ka Siong had questioned why there was no uproar from Pakatan Harapan when Peter was released under parole, contrasting this with the coalition’s call for those convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, to serve their sentences in full.
The issue comes amid renewed attention on former prime minister Najib Razak’s bid for a pardon over his convictions linked to the 1MDB scandal.
a3b27e5b4203d877: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) is expected to return home from Nepal today or tomorrow, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
Mohamad, who is also Umno deputy president, said the team would leave behind the drones it had brought from Malaysia for use by Nepalese rescue teams.
"However, they will leave and hand over all the drones brought from here to the Nepalese rescue teams for them to use," he said on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno general assembly today.
Mohamad said Nepalese authorities had no immediate plans to announce the end of their search and rescue operation, with about 5,000 people still unaccounted for.
He said the authorities were reluctant to formally end the operation as they did not want to trigger public pressure or unrest.
"According to the daily reports from our embassy, the Nepalese authorities have no intention of announcing the end of the search and rescue operation.

"There are still about 5,000 people who remain unaccounted for, and they are trying not to announce the termination of the search and rescue operation because they do not want local issues to arise, as they fear the people will pressure the Nepalese Government and others," he said.
Asked whether Malaysia would deploy a second SMART team to Nepal, Mohamad said the decision would be made following an assessment by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma).
He said Malaysia did not want to rush into making a decision on further deployment.
"That should be left to the SMART team chief or Nadma to report and assess our next move.
"We do not want to rush or make a hasty decision. Let SMART and Nadma assess the situation and report to the government on the next step, including whether we should continue," he said.
He said search efforts remained challenging due to thick layers of mud and sand that had buried entire houses and buildings.
He said Nepalese security and rescue teams would continue to manage the search, while Malaysia remained ready to provide assistance if requested.
"If they (Nepal authorities) need assistance from Malaysia, we can contribute and provide whatever help is needed for rescue or search operations."
The SMART team departed for Nepal on Sept 5 to assist in a humanitarian mission following devastating floods that hit the country.
Mohamad said authorities had identified the last known location of the 55 Malaysians who remained unaccounted for through their mobile phone signals.
"We have the last ping from their phones that we were able to identify, and that location was among the worst-hit areas affected by the tsunami," he said.
More than two weeks since devastating floods struck the Nepal-China border region, the fate of 55 Malaysians who remain unreachable is still unknown.
The disaster has killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.

af0f84cb9c5eac55: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A lawyer for former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has reportedly denied claims that the government forfeited RM18 million held in TH accounts belonging to his family members.

According to New Straits Times, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad also rejected claims that savings belonging to Azeez’s wife and children were linked to TH funds, saying such allegations — which were posted on social media — were not related to the criminal charge faced by his client.
He reportedly said in a press statement that Azeez was not charged with taking, misappropriating or misusing the RM193.5 million mentioned in the case for himself or his family.

Instead, Amer reportedly said the charge read out at the Sessions Court on September 8 alleged that Azeez used his position as TH chairman to obtain the chairmanship of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, which brought benefits including annual remuneration, a vehicle and a permanent driver.

“The RM193.5 million mentioned in the charge is the value of TH’s investment in Putrajaya Perdana Bhd and not money alleged to have been given to, taken by or deposited into the personal accounts of our client or his family members,” Amer was quoted as saying.

He added that the family’s TH accounts had previously been investigated by the authorities, but the savings had never been forfeited by the government or found to be misappropriated TH funds or proceeds of illegal activities.

Amer also reportedly said the Royal Commission of Inquiry into TH had made no finding that Azeez had taken or misappropriated TH funds for himself or his family, adding that Azeez has pleaded not guilty to the charge.
He said Azeez and his family reserved the right to take legal action against anyone who published or spread false, misleading or defamatory statements over the matter.

The charge against Azeez relates to an alleged offence at a TH board meeting on August 25, 2014, and was framed under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine upon conviction.

His prosecution is among several cases involving former TH officials following the release in July of the Royal Commission of Inquiry report into the pilgrimage fund’s management, which flagged a number of problematic investments, including the Putrajaya Perdana deal.
055c10741bf5ee15: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is committed to strengthening regional cooperation in the field of renewable energy and connectivity as an effort to expand economic opportunities at the sub-regional level of Asean, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.

He said that sub-regional approaches such as the Indonesia-Malaysia-Thailand Growth Triangle (IMT-GT) can strengthen the economic potential among member countries through the implementation of more structured and effective plans.

“At the Malaysian level, we acknowledge the implementation we have carried out for the blueprint until 2026, and at this moment, we are planning the next blueprint from 2027 to 2031 before moving towards the IMT-GT Vision 2036,” he said at a press conference while attending the 32nd IMT-GT Ministerial Meeting in Medan, Indonesia.

The meeting was held on Sept 10, under the chairmanship of Indonesian Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartanto, and attended by Thailand’s Vice Minister for Office of the Prime Minister Dr Thanadit Raktabutr.

According to Akmal Nasrullah, one of the main focuses includes strengthening the renewable energy sector through initiatives such as the Asean Power Grid, as well as enhancing the level of physical connectivity between Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand.
He said that the close geographical proximity between Kuala Lumpur and Medan needs to be fully utilised to accelerate economic integration.
At the same time, Akmal Nasrullah also emphasised the importance of sustainability and digital agendas as new growth drivers, including expanding opportunities in the green economy in the sub-region.
He also expressed Malaysia’s readiness to host the IMT-GT meeting in September 2027 in Langkawi.
Meanwhile, in a joint statement, the ministers reaffirmed their commitment to the IMT-GT Vision 2036, which aims to create an integrated, innovative, inclusive, and sustainable subregion.
They noted that amid geopolitical uncertainties and growing trade fragmentation, there is a pressing need to strengthen resilience and capacity to respond to external disruptions.
The ministers also recognised artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation as strategic enablers of productivity, innovation, and competitiveness.

“In this regard, we remain committed to deepening cooperation across the three Focus Areas of Agriculture and Agro-based Industry, Tourism, and Halal Products and Services, supported by the five Enabler Focus Areas, to strengthen resilience and promote shared prosperity,” they said.

The joint statement further highlighted achievements under the IMT-GT Implementation Blueprint (IB) 2022-2026, particularly in gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, foreign direct investment (FDI), and international visitor arrivals, which surpassed the 2026 targets.
The GDP per capita increased from 21,646 current PPP$ in 2024 to 23,290 in 2025, while total trade in goods rose from US$708 billion (RM2.88 trillion) to US$810.8 billion (RM3.30 trillion).

FDI inflows increased from US$27.52 billion (RM112.1 billion) to US$28.44 billion (RM115.9 billion), while the unemployment rate declined from 3.8 per cent to 3.7 per cent, reflecting the subregion’s economic resilience.

“To address remaining gaps, we emphasise that the IB 2027-2031 should be anchored on three strategic goals - Economic Resilience, Integrated Networks, and Shared Prosperity - supported by stronger institutional coordination, stakeholder engagement, and robust monitoring and evaluation towards the achievement of Vision 2036,” it said. — Bernama

a10f9a3931ba8af4: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is seeking to send DNA experts to Nepal or have samples taken from victims recovered there sent to Kuala Lumpur to help identify Malaysians still missing following the disaster, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
Mohamad, who is also Umno deputy president, said Malaysia was negotiating with the Nepalese authorities on the matter as the country lacked the facilities and equipment needed for DNA testing.

"We are also negotiating to send DNA experts to examine the samples, or we want to ask them to send the DNA samples taken from victims who have been found so that it will be easier for us to identify them or conduct DNA matching.

"They lack facilities, equipment and other resources there. So, through our embassy, we have asked whether the Nepalese authorities could send the samples to Malaysia, to Kuala Lumpur, so that we can conduct matching with the next of kin whose DNA samples have already been taken," he said on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Mohamad said Malaysia was also seeking clarification from the Nepalese Foreign and Law ministries on the legal status of Malaysians who remained missing.
He said Nepal only allowed death certificates to be issued three years after a missing person could not be located, compared with seven years in Malaysia.
"If possible, we want to negotiate so that matters such as insurance and others can be settled immediately.

"That is why we have asked our embassy there to engage with the Nepalese Law Ministry on how next of kin can obtain any documents that can confirm the disappearance of Malaysians who, to date, cannot be found," he said.
More than two weeks after devastating floods struck the Nepal-China border region, the fate of 55 Malaysians who remain unreachable is still unknown.

fc54d34fa8c64218: MELAKA: A gold bracelet worth about RM15,000 could have been a windfall for a gardener, but Tengku Andy Asmawi Tengku Ahamad chose to do what he believed was right and return it to its owner.
The 28-year-old found the 25g gold bracelet while sweeping the grounds of the Maritime Museum in Banda Hilir last Sunday.
Instead of keeping the jewellery, he immediately handed it over to the museum management.
Tengku Andy Asmawi said that when he found the gold corn bracelet, he did not think about its value but regarded it as his responsibility to return it to its rightful owner.
"I was sweeping as usual when I noticed what looked like a gold bracelet. I then handed it to a museum staff member.
"At the time, I did not think about whether the item was expensive. What mattered was my responsibility at work," he said when met at the Maritime Museum.
He said the bracelet did not belong to him and therefore had to be returned to its rightful owner.
He added that he worked to provide for his family and did not want to take something that belonged to someone else.
"I earn a living for my wife and children, and my wife often reminds me to do my job properly. If we find someone else's belongings, we have to return them," he said.
Tengku Andy Asmawi, who is from Kemaman, Terengganu, said he previously worked at Wisma Negeri Terengganu before resigning and accepting an opportunity to work as a gardener at the museum.
He said he made the decision because he no longer wanted to live apart from his wife and their two children, aged three years and three months.
"My wife and I used to live apart, and I am grateful for the opportunity to work in Melaka. At least I can be closer to my family while earning a living here," he said.
He said the bracelet was found at about 7am while he was carrying out his routine duty of sweeping.
Meanwhile, Melaka Museum Corporation assistant curator of management Farahwahidah Abd Wahab said it became aware of the missing bracelet after being contacted by a visitor from Kuala Lumpur.
She said the visitor sought the museum's assistance in case the bracelet was found before informing others about the matter through a WhatsApp group.
"We were then informed that the gold bracelet had been found by a gardener and subsequently handed over to the museum," she said.
1e6e7768fec3d04e: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Kedah menamakan PAS sebagai parti untuk perbincangan kerjasama politik bagi menghadapi PRU16, dan menolak Perikatan Nasional.
Ketua Penerangan Shaiful Hazizy Zainal Abidin mengumumkan Umno Kedah akan memulakan perbincangan dengan PAS dan tidak dengan PN.

"Kita akan memulakan 'minum kopi' kita dengan parti PAS, tetapi tidak dengan PN sebab di dalam PN ada 'parti kucing', parti yang baru dua hari ditubuhkan," katanya ketika berucap membahaskan ucapan dasar presiden pada Perhimpunan Agung Umno 2026 di Pusat Dagangan Dunia Kuala Lumpur.

Berhubung 'parti kucing' yang diperkatakan itu, Shaiful tidak menamakan mana-mana pihak dan menjelaskan beliau menggunakan istilah yang disebut oleh Ketua Pengarah Pilihan Raya PAS, Sanusi Nor, ketika muktamar tahunan PAS baru-baru ini.

Pada 5 Sept lalu, Sanusi mengumumkan PAS tidak mahu lagi menyerahkan kerusi yang berpotensi dimenangi kepada parti lain pada pilihan raya akan datang, mengatakan PAS sudah terlalu lama berdepan keadaan di mana kekuatan dan sokongan yang dimiliki tidak diterjemahkan sepenuhnya kepada penguasaan politik.

Sanusi juga berkata PAS perlu berhenti berasa rendah diri ketika berunding dengan parti lain, mengatakan PAS dengan sejarah politik yang panjang dan kekuatan yang besar tidak patut ikut 'parti kucing' yang baru sahajd ditubuhkan.

Dalam perkembangan sama, Timbalan Presiden Umno, Mohamad Hasan, memaklumkan kepada pemberita bahawa Umno Kedah bebas membuat 'apa sahaja perbincangan' di peringkat negeri memandangkan Umno tidak boleh menggunakan satu formula untuk semua negeri.

"Apa jua perbincangan mereka itu mereka perlu bawa ke pengetahuan ibu pejabat dan tiba masanya nanti pengurusan di ibu pejabat akan meneliti setiap apa jua rundingan perbincangan yang dilakukan," katanya di tepian PAU 2026.
92589cd9ba082145: SEPT 12 — As Malaysians prepare to mark Malaysia Day on September 16, the wreckage at Long Lellang Airport offers a sobering starting point for reflection.

On September 8, a helicopter carrying a medical team from the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) crashed in Ulu Baram, Sarawak, killing all five people on board: the pilot, a medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses.

The decision by the Health Ministry (KKM) to suspend all FDS operations in Sarawak pending a review of safety, governance and the service delivery model was necessary and appropriate. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad has said the review will cover contracts, governance, operational safety, coverage requirements and the effectiveness of the existing model. In the interim, emergency evacuations will continue in cooperation with the Fire and Rescue Department, while discussions proceed with the Armed Forces over possible backup transport.

Necessary though that response is, it also exposes an uncomfortable reality: a single incident can reveal just how thin the safety net is on which rural Sarawak has depended for more than five decades. As of April 2026, the FDS served 97 localities across the interior regions of Kapit, Miri and Limbang. Most were visited only once a month, and some only once every two months, depending on operational capacity.
63 years of equal partnership?
As Malaysia marks 63 years since the formation of the federation, it is worth asking plainly whether equal partnership has translated into equal access to a doctor.

In Putrajaya, healthcare is often no more complicated than getting into a car and driving to the nearest hospital. In Ulu Baram, however, reaching the same care can depend on a chain of contingencies: whether a leased helicopter is airworthy, whether the weather permits flying, and whether an operator has both an aircraft and crew available to make the journey.

That disparity reflects a policy reality that has remained largely unchanged for decades. In some of Malaysia’s most remote communities, access to healthcare still depends on extraordinary measures rather than ordinary, resilient infrastructure.

Seen in that light, the FDS is both a lifeline and a reminder. It provides essential care to communities that might otherwise go without it, while also underscoring a problem that successive governments have never fully resolved.
A stopgap that became permanent

This is not an argument for assigning blame to any particular government. The FDS has persisted, and remained necessary, across successive administrations because the underlying challenge, geographic isolation without adequate road or scheduled air transport alternatives, has never been comprehensively addressed.

But the service’s longevity is itself revealing. Introduced in Sarawak in 1973 to bridge a profound gap in rural healthcare, the FDS remains, 53 years later, a principal means by which many remote communities gain access to medical care.

A stopgap can be defended in the short term. It is harder to continue treating it as temporary after half a century. 63 years of federation should have been long enough to move rural healthcare beyond a service re-tendered every few years and towards resilient infrastructure planned in decades rather than contract cycles.

If that sounds demanding, it is worth remembering that Malaysia is hardly the first country to confront the challenge of delivering healthcare across vast and sparsely populated terrain. The question is not whether such access can be sustained, but how a country chooses to sustain it.
What Australia got right

Australia’s Royal Flying Doctor Service, founded in 1928 and funded by the Australian government since the 1930s, offers an instructive model, not simply for the aircraft it operates, but for the institutional architecture that supports them.

For decades, agreements between the RFDS and the Australian government ran for only four years at a time. In 2022, that approach gave way to a decade-long strategic partnership worth close to A$1 billion (about RM2.9 billion), covering the period from 2022–23 to 2031–32. In December 2024, Canberra reinforced that commitment by announcing an additional A$74.8 million over three years and reaffirming its long-term partnership with the RFDS.

Crucially, the arrangement requires the RFDS to conduct a formal needs assessment every 3 years. This helps ensure that services are directed towards documented coverage gaps rather than having their necessity repeatedly contested through short-term budget cycles.

The approach has supported one of the world’s largest remote healthcare networks. The RFDS records more than 345,000 patient contacts annually through clinics, aeromedical transport and telehealth consultations.
More important than its scale, however, is what the model represents: remote healthcare is treated as a permanent national responsibility and supported through a long-term institutional framework.
The lesson for Malaysia is not the size of Australia’s fleet or the scale of its budget. It is the policy discipline of planning beyond the next contract cycle.
Financing equity, not just flights

A significant first step would be to move the FDS beyond the uncertainty of short-term leasing arrangements and annual competition for funding. In their place should be a multiyear, ring-fenced funding framework tied to published assessments of community needs.

A 3-year review cycle, similar to the RFDS model, would help ensure that future allocations respond to documented coverage gaps rather than shifting budget priorities. It would also provide a clearer basis for evaluating whether existing routes, visit frequencies and transport arrangements remain adequate as communities and healthcare needs change.
Such a review should not be the responsibility of KKM alone. In remote communities where access to healthcare depends on aviation, health policy and transport policy are inseparable.

The Ministry of Transport, aviation regulators, the Sarawak government, emergency services and airport operators should all have a role in assessing capacity, identifying vulnerabilities and planning for future demand. Potential cooperation with state-linked aviation providers such as AirBorneo could also be examined as part of a broader review, rather than assumed in advance.

Just as importantly, redundancy should be treated as a deliberate feature of the system rather than an avoidable expense. Whether achieved through a second operator, supplementary transport arrangements, shared access to government assets or a dedicated contingency mechanism, resilience carries a cost. But so does dependence on a single point of failure.

None of these measures would eliminate the challenges of geography. Weather would still disrupt flights, remote settlements would remain difficult to reach, and aviation would continue to carry inherent risks. But better funding, coordination and contingency planning would reduce the extent to which access to healthcare depends on a single aircraft, a single operator or the timing of the next procurement exercise.
For communities that continue to rely on the Flying Doctor Service, that would represent meaningful progress.
A promise still owed

Budgets, contracts and governance frameworks, however important, are ultimately means rather than ends. What matters is whether they enable people in remote communities to receive care when they need it.

These questions matter because they affect communities that rarely feature in national debates except in moments of crisis. The five lives lost at Long Lellang were given in service of a basic promise: that every Malaysian, regardless of where they live, deserves a fair chance of seeing a doctor.

As the country marks another Malaysia Day, that promise remains only partially fulfilled. Malaysia does not lack the fiscal capacity to do better, nor does it lack examples of what sustained commitment can achieve. What has been missing is the decision to treat rural healthcare access as permanent national infrastructure, planned and funded over decades rather than renewed contract by contract.

The true test of that commitment will not be another review, inquiry or statement of condolence. It will be whether a parent in a remote longhouse can seek care for a sick child with the same certainty as a parent in Putrajaya, without first wondering whether an aircraft is available, whether the weather will hold, or whether help can arrive at all.
* Dr Mohd Zaidi Md Zabri is a Research Fellow at the Centre for Islamic Economics, Kulliyyah of Economics and Management Sciences, International Islamic University Malaysia.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
09a0983199b89b43: SINGAPORE, Sept 12 — More than 600 luxury items forfeited in Singapore’s largest money laundering case are going under the hammer, including a 15-carat yellow diamond ring and a pink enamel clutch shaped like a serpent’s head.

CNA reported that auction house Hotlotz will conduct 15 online auctions from this month through May 2027, following the seizure and forfeiture of more than 1,000 items and 80 properties linked to the case.
The case came to light after island-wide raids in August 2023 uncovered millions of dollars linked to an illicit gambling operation based in South-east Asia.
The luxury goods are now available for online bidding, with viewing sessions beginning next Monday and running until Saturday, although appointments are required and walk-ins are not permitted.
“The response has been overwhelmingly good,” Hotlotz co-founder and director of auctions Christopher Lanigan O’Keeffe said during a media preview on Thursday.
He said viewing slots had been filling quickly, with almost all of the roughly 75 appointments available each day already booked.

As of Thursday evening, the highest handbag bid was S$39,000 for a limited-edition Louis Vuitton Yayoi Kusama leather pumpkin bag, against an estimated value of S$12,000 to S$16,000. — Screengrab from CNA
The first two auctions, covering jewellery, handbags and accessories, have combined pre-sale estimates of between S$2.9 million (RM9.3 million) and S$3.9 million.

The first auction, which closes at 4pm on September 20, includes items from Chanel, Louis Vuitton and Christian Dior, while the second, ending at the same time on September 27, features jewellery by Graff, Bulgari and Van Cleef & Arpels.
The seized goods were transferred to Hotlotz about four months ago after the auction house was appointed to conduct the sales, and are being stored at Le Freeport, a high-security facility in Changi.

Hotlotz said the items had previously been held by auditing firm Deloitte and the Singapore Police Force, while specialists assessed each piece for authenticity, condition and factors affecting its value.
A 15.02-carat yellow diamond ring had attracted a top bid of S$190,000 against an estimate of S$200,000 to S$300,000. — Screengrab from CNA

As of Thursday evening, the highest handbag bid was S$39,000 for a limited-edition Louis Vuitton Yayoi Kusama leather pumpkin bag, against an estimated value of S$12,000 to S$16,000, while a 15.02-carat yellow diamond ring had attracted a top bid of S$190,000 against an estimate of S$200,000 to S$300,000.

Among the other high-value pieces is a 30-carat Hermes Kelly diamond bracelet containing 263 diamonds, which is estimated at S$150,000 to S$200,000 and had received a top bid of S$80,000 as of Thursday.
Lanigan O’Keeffe said it was difficult to predict whether the high-profile nature of the case would affect demand, noting that the value buyers place on an item’s provenance varies.
The 10 offenders involved in the case, all originally from China, have been convicted and deported after serving their sentences.
“With this particular case, we weren’t sure what the response would be, given the nature of the case. But we’ve seen a great response so far,” he said.
7b9eff86adc3de69: KUALA LUMPUR: The 16th General Election should be held earlier due to increasingly strained ties between Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan, an Umno Supreme Council member said.
Pontian member of Parliament Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said GE16 should be held as soon as possible, preferably concurrently with the Melaka or Sarawak state elections.
"This would be the best option compared with the 'tebuk atap' attempt, which has been rejected by BN," he said.
He said there were also other "turning points" that had made Umno and BN feel increasingly uncomfortable in the unity government, necessitating an earlier GE16.
This included the way leaders from the party were treated in prosecutions, he said.
"The relationship between the unity government and Umno is now, I would say, at a rather uncomfortable stage, with several turning points that we have seen taking place.
"PH, which is the core party in the government, has lost three state elections, and some quarters predict it could lose in Melaka and Sarawak.
"This clearly reflects the people's lack of confidence in the government's core party," he said.
"As such, the mandate should be returned to the people to choose," Ahmad added.

Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, in his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly yesterday, reiterated his call for GE16 to be held earlier, before the term of the 15th Parliament expires next year.

Ahmad, who is also deputy works minister, said that based on the mood among leaders and the grassroots at the party's general assembly, he believed cooperation between BN and PH for any election, including the Melaka election, would not materialise.

"From a political logic standpoint, how could we not understand the president's speech? We have to understand it, especially with the invitation extended to Pas, in addition to the many veiled remarks," he said.
Asked whether Umno and BN should leave the unity government, Ahmad said such a major decision could only be determined through the Umno General Assembly and a meeting of the Umno Supreme Council.

On Zahid's call in his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly for the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to be reintroduced, Ahmad said the tax system could contribute up to RM100 billion a year to the country.
He said he had also been informed during a recent budget dialogue session by the Finance Ministry that several parties wanted GST to be reintroduced.
"My PhD (Doctor of Philosophy) is on GST, and to date, 176 countries, or 90 per cent of all countries in the world, have implemented GST, with some doing so as early as the 1950s.
"Surely 90 per cent of countries cannot be wrong. If GST had not been abolished, the country could have collected up to RM100 billion a year.
"It is very strange that no country has implemented a hybrid system for taxation," he said.
4be97d3c155621b9: KUALA LUMPUR: Kedah Umno will begin discussions with PAS over possible political cooperation but will not negotiate with Perikatan Nasional, says a party division chief.

Merbok Umno chief Shaiful Hazizy Zainol Abidin told the Umno general assembly today this was because PN includes a party he dismissed as "the cat", a description he attributed to Kedah menteri besar Sanusi Nor, who is also PAS's election director.
Shaiful also described Umno and smaller parties using animal comparisons, saying Sanusi had previously described Umno as the “elephant” and the other side as the “cat”.

“Sanusi was the one who said we would not negotiate with a ‘dwarf party’. We are the elephant party, while they (the PN component) are the cat party,” he said during the debate on the president's policy speech.
"This party is causing trouble. So Kedah Umno will not negotiate with the cat party'. We will negotiate with PAS."
Shaiful did not name the party he was referring to, but he went on to criticise elected representatives who had quit Bersatu to join Wawasan.
“Datuk Seri president, Kedah Umno wishes to express some concern about certain groups,” he said, addressing Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
"Suddenly, the elected representative for a constituency announces resignation and joins Wawasan. Kedah Umno sees this as buying insurance at the last minute."
However, Shaiful said Kedah Umno would ultimately leave it to Zahid to decide on the party’s broader political direction.
It was previously reported that Kedah Umno chairman Mahdzir Khalid was planning to meet Sanusi to discuss possible cooperation ahead of the 16th general election.

Umno failed to win a single parliamentary seat in Kedah during the 2022 general election and was wiped out of the assembly in the state election the following year. PAS holds the lion’s share of both parliamentary and state seats in Kedah.
Sanusi said at PAS's recent muktamar the party would no longer give up winnable seats to other parties in future elections.
fbf94b5fdb37d523: KUALA LUMPUR: Rain and heavy traffic did little to dampen the warm atmosphere inside Barra Restaurant on Wednesday, where Spanish diplomats, chefs, and food lovers gathered to celebrate a shared appreciation for good food.
For Spain's Ambassador-designate to Malaysia Sergi Farré Salvá, food offers a natural connection between Spain and Malaysia, a country where eating is deeply woven into everyday life.

"One of the first words that we learn when we come here in Bahasa Melayu is makan," said Farré, who arrived in Malaysia a month ago. "So, we are going to do lots of makan-makan today," he added, drawing laughter from the guests.
Farré called food a "universal connector" and described his first dining experience at Barra as more than simply a meal.
"It was a cultural experience, an artistic experience," he said, highlighting the combination of tradition, creativity, and innovation that characterises Spanish gastronomy.
The ambassador-designate is expected to present his credentials to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, in late October or early November this year.
During the event, Farré officially presented the Restaurants From Spain certification plaque to Chef Gabriel Bonin, Chef Ignasi Prats, and the Barra team.

Awarded by the Spanish government through ICEX Spain Trade and Investment, the certification recognises restaurants outside Spain that offer authentic, high-quality Spanish cuisine and promote Spanish culinary products and culture.
Farré said the certification was reserved for outstanding establishments and Barra's inclusion had brought the number of certified Spanish restaurants in Kuala Lumpur to eight.
"That says a lot about Malaysia and what this capital stands for. Food happens 24 hours a day, seven days a week here. It is a paradise for any food lover," he said.
He said Spain's culinary reputation was built not only on its centuries-old heritage and the influence of civilisations across the Mediterranean, but also on continuous innovation.
"You cannot have this level of gastronomy without innovation, science, and technology that cooks and chefs like Gabriel and Ignasi bring," he said.

The Embassy of Spain in Malaysia's Chief Economic and Commercial Counsellor Juan Guía said the gathering served two objectives: to celebrate Barra's certification and formally introduce the second edition of the Eat Spain Drink Spain festival in Malaysia.
He said the campaign sought to make Spanish food more accessible to Malaysians while encouraging people to discover it together with their families and friends.
"Spanish gastronomy is known globally for its creativity and diversity, and for being deeply rooted in our history and heritage.
"Eat Spain Drink Spain is about bringing our gastronomy to Malaysia for locals to enjoy and discover with their friends and families," he said.
The festival, scheduled from Sept 18 to Oct 4, will take place in more than 40 participating venues across Malaysia, including Kuala Lumpur, Melaka, Johor, Penang, and Kuching.

The embassy's foreign trade and investment official Andrea Lázaro said participating establishments would offer a variety of experiences, including two-week promotional menus, weekend pop-ups, and one-day tapas events.
Some venues will highlight traditional favourites such as paella, tortilla de patatas, and Basque cheesecake, while others will present more contemporary interpretations of Spanish cuisine.

Lázaro clarified that Eat Spain Drink Spain is a separate initiative from the Restaurants From Spain certification. Eat Spain Drink Spain is an annual international festival organised by ICEX in which restaurants and other venues host their own Spanish food and beverage events.
Barra, which opened in April 2024, is a restaurant under The Tamarind Restaurants group which Guía described as a "piece of Barcelona" in one of Kuala Lumpur's Chinese neighbourhoods.
The group's restaurants and dining concepts in the Kuala Lumpur area were founded and conceptualised by Federico
Asaro, chief executive officer and driving force behind Samadhi Retreats.
Guía also credited Prats and Bonin for building Barra's identity.
Bonin said the certification carried both pride and responsibility for the restaurant's team.
"We are really proud to be part of the Spanish community, to show Spain to the world and to show our gastronomy.
"It is a big challenge for us, but at the same time, receiving this recognition keeps us giving our best."
