7f3cab2b9609ad68: LOS ANGELES: Grammy-winning rap artist Lil Durk was acquitted on Friday of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire case accusing him of orchestrating the revenge killing of a man shot dead in a daytime ambush in Los Angeles four years ago.

Two co-defendants tried with the recording artist, whose real name is Durk Banks, were acquitted of murder-for-hire-related charges but were found guilty on charges of conspiracy to commit stalking, as well as stalking with a dangerous weapon and stalking resulting death.

Although Banks was found not guilty of all those charges, he remains in custody and faces a separate trial scheduled for Oct 5 on murder-related racketeering and weapons offenses, according to a spokesman for the US Attorney's Office in Los Angeles.
His two co-defendants, Deandre Dontrell Wilson and David Brian Lindsey, face trial on the same counts.

According to a 32-page federal indictment filed in the case, Banks is the ringleader of a violent criminal gang consisting of associates from his rap music label, One of the Family, that has engaged in robbery, murder and drug trafficking.
The trial that ended on Friday stemmed from a fatal shooting on August 2022 at a gasoline station near the Beverly Center shopping mall in Los Angeles that prosecutors described as a planned hit.

Banks, 33, who won the 2024 Grammy for best melodic rap performance for his hit single "All My Life", was accused of ordering, financing and masterminding the intended murder of a rival rapper Quando Rondo, born Tyquian Bowman.

According to prosecutors, Banks placed a bounty on Bowman's head as revenge for the killing two years earlier of a close friend of Banks, Dayvon "King Von" Bennett, by one of Bowman's associates in an Atlanta nightclub.
But the squad of killers who Banks allegedly sent to hunt down Bowman ended up killing Bowman's 24-year-old cousin, Saviay'a Robinson, by mistake, in a hail of gunfire.
Banks, who was arrested in October 2024 at a Florida airport after five other suspects were charged in the case, has pleaded not guilty to all charges.

Defense lawyers have asserted that Banks had nothing to do with the plot, maintaining that it was a former personal assistant who ordered the hit to impress his boss, the Los Angeles City News Service reported in its account of the trial.
The ex-assistant and two other Banks associates originally indicted with the rapper reached plea deals in the case and testified for the prosecution, according to CNS.
Banks' acquittal set off a celebration by the rap artist's supporters outside the downtown Los Angeles federal courthouse where the trial was held.
977e8c9469a427ee: NEW YORK, Sept 12 — Big-serving Ben Shelton overpowered American compatriot Frances Tiafoe in four sets to reach the first Grand Slam final of his career at the US Open on Friday.

Eighth-seeded Shelton blasted 20 aces on his way to a thrilling 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 victory on the Arthur Ashe Stadium court that sends the 23-year-old into Sunday’s championship match against top-seeded Alexander Zverev of Germany.
A pulsating all-American semi-final had seen both players vying to reach a Grand Slam final for the first time.

Shelton — who took down defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals — will now have the chance to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam title since 2003, when Andy Roddick triumphed at the US Open.
Tiafoe got off to a bright start, claiming the first set after breaking when Shelton uncharacteristically double-faulted to trail at 5-4.
Tiafoe held to love to clinch the first set but Shelton came flying out of the blocks to start the second.
An early break helped him into a 2-0 lead before Tiafoe responded with a break to level at 2-2.
Yet with Tiafoe’s serve increasingly erratic, Shelton grabbed another break in the eighth game to go 5-3 up and then held to level.
The momentum was all with Shelton and Tiafoe had to fight off two break points before holding early in the third set.
However Shelton – who had one serve initially clocked at 158mph before it was later adjusted to 144mph — made no mistake in the fifth game with a break to go 3-2 up.
Tiafoe needed to hold to keep the set alive in the ninth game, and a furious arm-wrestle saw the 11th seed once again save three break and set points.
Shelton though earned his fourth break point after pouncing on Tiafoe’s second serve once more, scorching a backhand return down the line.
Shelton converted that when Tiafoe netted a forehand to find himself 2-1 down.
The fourth set went with serve until the 12th game, when Shelton grabbed the crucial break to seal victory. — AFP
8ba51419ea34947e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Pokémon fans turned out in droves for both the 30th anniversary of Pokémon celebration at KLCC Park as well as the opening of Malaysia’s first Pokémon Centre Pop-up Store, alongside the Nintendo Pop-up at nearby Ombak KLCC.
Despite queues for the pop-up only opening at 6am, fans had already been lingering near the Ombak KLCC site since the night before.
Malay Mail sighted a long queue snaking around the building by 7.30am roughly 70-80 strong.
According to the organisers, the queue was not to enter the store but to receive tickets for specific slots for entry<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Pokémon fans Yap, Debbie and Shi Lin made their way early to Ombak KLCC just to acquire tickets to enter the pop-up store. (Left to right, clockwise). — Picture by Erna Mahyuni
Each ticket allows the holder to stay a maximum of 20 minutes with some items such as the exclusive Malaysia turquoise-haired Pikachu mascot plushie limited to one per person.
Before 9.30am, slots for the entire morning and afternoon session had been fully booked with slots for the night sessions only opening at 7 or 8pm.
Staff confirmed that fans would not be allowed to queue earlier than the stipulated hours, no matter how early they arrived.
@ernamh A preview of what’s available at Malaysia’s first ever Pokémon Pop-up store. #pokemon #pokexciting KISS N TELL - aespa
Fun for the family

Qiqi and Zenki didn’t manage to get early tickets to the pop-up store but were thrilled to visit nevertheless. — Picture by Erna Mahyuni

4cc1eaa7bb16bbf7: KUALA LUMPUR: Muay Thai exponent Rabiatul Adawiyah Yunus won the gold medal in the women's under-24 48kg category at the IFMA World Senior Muaythai Championships in Kosovo on Friday, strengthening her chances of representing Malaysia at next year's SEA Games.

Marshall Jaydden Jerry took gold in the men's Wai Kru discipline, adding to his earlier victory at the IFMA World Invitational Muaythai Championship here.
In the men's 54kg Ring Combat category, 2025 Thailand SEA Games gold medallist Wassof Rumijam earned a silver medal after losing to world champion Hamza Eren of Turkiye in the final.
Nur Arisya Sofea also took silver in the women's 45kg Ring Combat final after losing to Vietnam's Mai Hoang Khanh.
However, she bounced back in the Technical Muay Thai (Tatami) discipline, defeating India's Ayushree Banerjee to claim gold.

National coach Bernard Radin said he was satisfied with the performance of his 10 exponents in Kosovo, calling the tournament an ideal testing ground before selecting the squad for next year's SEA Games.
"However, mental strength needs continuous attention. Our athletes must have confidence when facing opponents with world champion status.
"The status and achievements of opponents should not cause our athletes to lose confidence before entering the ring.

"Preparations for the 2027 SEA Games will focus not only on physical and technical aspects, but also on mental toughness, confidence, and the ability to handle pressure on the international stage," Bernard added.
b72b466195faf9bf: KUCHING, Sept 12 — When a helicopter crashed just 200 metres from her home in Long Lellang, Renai Iwat was not only confronted with the trauma of losing a vital link to medical care, but also another race against time.

The dialysis patient, who requires treatment three times a week, needed to return to Miri after the Long Lellang STOLport was closed following Tuesday’s tragic helicopter crash that claimed the lives of four medical personnel and a pilot.
Amid the grief and uncertainty, her family turned to the authorities for help.
Renai was eventually airlifted from Long Lellang to Miri Hospital on Thursday (Sept 10) by a Bomba helicopter, allowing her to resume the treatment on which she depends.

A family member who wished to remain anonymous said the family would remain deeply grateful to Deputy Minister in the Premier’s Department (Labour, Immigration and Project Monitoring) Datuk Gerawat Gala, Miri Division Resident Tuan Galong Luang and Bomba for making the evacuation possible.
She said Gerawat had personally raised the urgency of bringing Renai back to Miri because of her dialysis schedule and had insisted that arrangements be made for her evacuation.

“Although we are deeply saddened by the loss of the four medical personnel and pilot in the tragic helicopter incident, Renai’s case shows how important the Flying Doctor Service is to our rural communities,” she told The Borneo Post when contacted.
She said the family’s concern was heightened by the fact that Renai had been at home when the helicopter crashed nearby.
“It was an extremely difficult situation for her and for all of us,” she said.
She also thanked Miri Health Department head Dr P Raviwharmman Packierisamy for supporting the request for Renai’s medical evacuation.
According to her, Galong then made the formal request to Bomba for the evacuation from Long Lellang to Miri, while the Bomba director approved the use of its helicopter.
She expressed particular appreciation to the helicopter captain and crew who flew back to Long Lellang to bring Renai safely to Miri.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Renai Iwat seated aboard the Bomba helicopter en route to Miri Hospital, accompanied by rescue personnel after her successful medical evacuation from Long Lellang. — The Borneo Post pic
For Renai, the evacuation was more than simply getting home.
It meant returning to hospital for treatment she needs three times a week and being reunited with her family after an ordeal that unfolded dangerously close to home.
Renai is the widow of the late Pemanca Freddy Abun, who served the Kelabit community for more than five years.

For the family, Renai’s experience underscored the importance of air medical services to communities in Sarawak’s remote interior, where access to healthcare can depend on the ability to travel by air.
The family also extended their condolences to the families of those who lost their lives in the crash.
They said Renai’s safe evacuation was a powerful reminder that for people living in remote communities, air medical services are not a luxury but a lifeline.
And for one family, that lifeline brought a mother, wife and grandmother safely home. — The Borneo Post
b355352d8e538827: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim's lawyer has denied allegations circulating on social media that the government had forfeited RM18 million in funds held in TH accounts belonging to his family members.
Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad also denied claims circulating on social media that savings in TH accounts belonging to Azeez's wife and children were linked to TH funds.
He said Azeez was not charged with taking, misappropriating or misusing RM193.5 million in TH funds for himself or his family.

"The charge read out at the Sessions Court (Criminal) 9 on Sept 8, 2026, relates to allegations that our client used his position as TH chairman to obtain the position of chairman of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, which allegedly brought benefits in the form of annual remuneration, a vehicle and a permanent driver.
"There is no mention in the charge of any misappropriation or misuse of TH funds for the benefit of our client or his family.

"The RM193.5 million mentioned in the charge is the value of TH's investment in Putrajaya Perdana Bhd and not money alleged to have been given to, taken by or deposited into the personal accounts of our client or his family members," he said in a statement.
He said Azeez had pleaded not guilty and maintained that the charge was untrue, adding that he had chosen to defend himself and seek a full trial in court.
He also addressed social media posts concerning the amount of savings allegedly held in TH accounts belonging to Azeez's wife and children.
"The savings in the TH accounts belonging to our client's wife and children have no connection with the charge faced by our client.

"It is also important to emphasise that the money in those accounts has no connection with TH funds or money belonging to TH. The mere existence of savings in TH accounts does not mean that the money originated from TH."
Amer Hamzah said the accounts and savings had previously been the subject of investigations by the authorities.

However, the savings in those accounts have never been forfeited by the government, and there has been no finding that the money was TH funds misappropriated by our client or proceeds from illegal activities, he said.
He said the Royal Commission of Inquiry report on TH did not find that Azeez had misappropriated or taken TH funds for himself or his family.

Amer Hamzah said Azeez and his family reserved all rights, including taking appropriate legal action against anyone who published or disseminated false, misleading or defamatory statements concerning the matter.
31ca617015ab14e5: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia’s Prisons Department said the release of former Sabah Infrastructure Minister Datuk Peter Anthony under the Licensed Prisoner Release Programme (PBSL) was granted after he met the required eligibility period and underwent the same screening and assessment process as other prisoners considered for the programme.
In a statement issued today, the department stressed that PBSL was not a cancellation, reduction or shortening of a court-imposed sentence.

“Prisoners granted PBSL continue to serve the remainder of their sentences, but do so in the community, subject to the conditions, regulations, supervision and monitoring of the Malaysian Prisons Department,” it said.

“To be considered for participation in PBSL, a prisoner must first meet the eligibility requirements, including having served at least one-third of the sentence. However, serving this minimum period does not automatically qualify a prisoner for release under PBSL,” it added.

Each candidate undergoes screening and assessment based on their conduct and character in prison, rehabilitation progress, participation in human development programmes, readiness to return to the community, family support, housing suitability, employment prospects and post-release monitoring needs.
At headquarters, applications are reviewed by a PBSL committee chaired by the Commissioner-General of Prisons and comprising senior officers and representatives from relevant agencies.

“Regarding the release of former Sabah Infrastructure Minister Datuk Peter Anthony, the Prisons Department stresses that consideration for his participation in PBSL was made after he reached the prescribed eligibility period and underwent the screening and assessment process applied to other candidates considered for the programme,” it said.

The department added that Anthony’s release did not mean that the remainder of his sentence had been waived. He would continue serving the balance of his sentence in the community and remain subject to the conditions, regulations and monitoring imposed throughout the period.
“An individual’s status is not a criterion that provides an advantage or exemption from the prescribed eligibility and assessment process,” the department added.
Peter Anthony was sentenced to three years in prison and fined RM50,000 after being convicted of falsifying documents linked to a Universiti Malaysia Sabah maintenance contract.
His conviction and sentence were upheld on appeal, and he began serving his sentence in March 2025 before being released under PBSL in March 2026.

MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong accused Pakatan Harapan of applying double standards by demanding full sentences for high-profile offenders while remaining silent when former Sabah minister Peter Anthony was released on parole after serving about a year of his three-year sentence.
0a9ae0245f52f418: MACAU, Sept 12 — Macau will hold its first national security trial behind closed doors next week, a court said on Friday, in a case against a former pro-democracy lawmaker charged with “subversion”.
The Chinese casino hub expanded the scope of national security laws in May 2023, and a new bill passed this year allows judges to hear national security cases behind closed doors.
Lawyers and rights groups have warned that the rule could undermine the functioning of government departments and apply to “any judicial case”.
Former Macau lawmaker Au Kam San in July 2025 became the first person to be arrested under the expanded law, with authorities alleging he had ties to foreign groups endangering China.
The judge decided to “hold the trial behind closed doors in order to ensure that national security interests are not compromised”, a statement released by Macau’s final appeals court said.

After Au’s arrest, details about the case remained scarce until this July, when judicial authorities in Macau confirmed that he would stand trial as a “principal offender” of subversion and other crimes.
The court said the trial decision had been confirmed by Macau’s national security committee, following a request from the city’s public prosecutions office.
The proceedings are set to begin September 16.
Au, 69, is a primary school teacher who became one of Macau’s longest-serving pro-democracy legislators before deciding not to seek re-election in 2021.
Authorities said that a court-appointed lawyer previously accepted by Au will continue to represent him.
Michael Polak, a London-based barrister representing Au, said Friday’s announcement showed “authorities are too embarrassed to have their evidence scrutinized by the Macau people or the press”.
“Au will be prevented from instructing an independent lawyer, which is a key provision of international law,” Polak told AFP.

He added: “In effect, he will be prosecuted by the Macau authorities, judged by the Macau authorities through a compliant judiciary and ‘defended’ by the Macau authorities through the national security committee-selected lawyer, which really outlines how farcical the process is.”
Au’s daughter Cherry said the family is not allowed to visit or communicate with him.
“All we ask for is a fair trial, due process, and for his more than three decades of dedication to the people of Macau not to be erased or forgotten,” she said in a statement in July.
Under Macau’s security law, subversion offences are subject to a prison term of up to 25 years. — AFP
58ef501ca4f9b660: KUALA LUMPUR: Kedah Umno will begin political cooperation talks with Pas, but not Perikatan Nasional (PN), said Kedah Umno information chief Datuk Shaiful Hazizy Zainol Abidin.
Shaiful said the state leadership had agreed to negotiate directly with Pas and would not engage with an unnamed PN component he described as a small party.

Shaiful said Kedah Umno would leave decisions on its political direction entirely to party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He appealed to Zahid to put Kedah Umno back on the political map, acknowledging uncertainty over how many seats it could seek in negotiations.

"Yesterday, the Perak representative said that through negotiations, Umno and Barisan Nasional in Perak could contest nine seats. Here in Kedah, we do not even know how many seats we can begin negotiations with."
Shaiful said Kedah Umno was election-ready, describing internal disagreements as minor and saying members would rally behind the party's candidates.
"When an election comes, we will come together. Our focus is to ensure our candidates win."
PN swept 33 of Kedah's 36 state seats in the 2023 state election, following its victory in 14 of the state's 15 parliamentary seats in the 2022 general election.
BN was wiped out in both elections, with Pakatan Harapan winning the remaining three state seats and the Sungai Petani parliamentary seat.
3388e2371f066b5e: HANOI: Pham Nhat Quan Anh, chairman of VinFast Auto Ltd, will take over as global chief executive officer of the Vietnamese electric vehicle maker, replacing his father and billionaire founder Pham Nhat Vuong amid an aggressive international push and growing losses.

Quan Anh was appointed chairman of VinFast in May and will now assume overall responsibility for the automaker’s global operations, according to a statement from parent company Vingroup. He will continue to serve as chairman and CEO of its Vietnam business.

The move comes as the company looks to expand across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and North America. VinFast posted a net loss of 28.1 trillion dong (US$1.1 billion) in the first quarter, 58.9% wider from a year ago as the company faces tough competition.

A graduate of Singapore Management University, Quan Anh has held senior roles at VinFast and other companies within the Vingroup conglomerate. He has been involved in VinFast’s development from its early expansion in Vietnam through its push into overseas markets. He will also retain his position as CEO of VinMetal, Vingroup’s steel manufacturing unit.

Vuong is promoting his other son to be global CEO of his electric ride-hailing taxi company, Green & Smart Mobility JSC. Pham Nhat Minh Hoang replaces Nguyen Quoc Tuan, who has been appointed global chairman, replacing Pham Thu Huong, Vuong’s wife.
The leadership reshuffling comes as both companies seek to accelerate overseas growth.
VinFast says it is now selling EVs in 16 countries, with vehicles and electric motorcycles produced at four factories across Vietnam, Indonesia and India.
GSM operates in seven countries and is weighing plans to expand into the US by the end of 2026, ahead of a planned Hong Kong initial public offering.
c77d4960fe8fd1e5: WASHINGTON, Sept 12 — The CIA released more than 70 presidential intelligence briefs related to Al-Qaeda and its leader Osama bin Laden on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks.

The release provides “unprecedented transparency on America’s most sensitive intelligence publication from the years before and the day after one of the darkest moments in our history,” the CIA said in a statement.

“The products trace the story of CIA analysts’ evolving understanding of Al-Qaeda and efforts to highlight and warn of Osama bin Laden’s attack plotting despite sparse, vague, and imperfect information,” it said.
A September 10, 1998 brief — parts of which were redacted — said that Al-Qaeda “may fly an explosive-packed airplane into a US city.”
Another dated December 4, 1998, which also contained redactions, said bin Laden “and his allies are preparing for attacks in the US, including an aircraft hijacking.”

The briefs cover a period starting during Bill Clinton’s presidency and continue into that of George W. Bush, who was in office when 19 Al-Qaeda operatives hijacked four airliners on September 11, 2001.
Two of the jets hit the World Trade Center’s Twin Towers, causing the iconic skyscrapers to collapse.
A third struck the Pentagon, while a fourth — believed to have been aiming for Congress or the White House — crashed into a field in Pennsylvania after passengers fought back.
The United States invaded Afghanistan and later Iraq as part of the so-called “War on Terror” after 9/11 — long-running wars that left tens of thousands of people dead. — AFP
62ff992deaad7ac0: MIRI, Sept 12 — The DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) test results for the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang in Baram have been obtained, and the remains will be handed over to the next of kin today, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah.
“Today, once the documentation is completed, the remains will be handed over to the families,” he told Bernama when contacted.
Meanwhile, funeral arrangements are under way for three of the five victims, as their families prepare to bid their final farewells.
Medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry will be laid to rest at the Anglican Cemetery in Lambir following a funeral service at the Good Shepherd Church in Lutong at 9 am on Sept 15.
His sister, Annastasia Luyah, said in a funeral notice shared on her Facebook last night that a wake will be held on Sept 14 at their family residence at Taman Desa Senadin here.

The wake for staff nurse Jessie Paya Jok will be held at Taman Wang Lusut while the body of staff nurse Debra Moset will be brought home to Kampung Semadang in Padawan, Kuching, for a wake service. The burial dates have yet to be announced.
All five people on board the BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace were killed after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at about 3.40 pm on Sept 8.
The other two who lost their lives were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin and pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham.
Dr Ainul is expected to be laid to rest at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery in Kelantan, while Captain Zainol will be brought home to Negeri Sembilan for burial.

Yesterday Mohamad Zainal said post-mortem examinations on all five victims were completed at the Forensic Department of Miri Hospital on Thursday night and the DNA analysis was expected to be completed today. — Bernama
300955334f42ddb3: TAMBUNAN: Stress over a divorce and a dispute is believed to have driven a 31-year-old man to murder his 56-year-old mother at a house in Kampung Katagayan yesterday.
Keningau police chief Superintendent Erwansyah Abdul Basir said preliminary investigations revealed that the man was emotionally distressed after separating from his wife.
He said the suspect, who is believed to have used a knife to murder his mother, has been remanded for seven days.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years upon conviction.
If the death penalty is not imposed, the offence also carries mandatory whipping of not less than 12 strokes of the rotan.
"Investigations are ongoing to determine the exact cause of the misunderstanding between the suspect and the victim," he said when contacted.
It was reported earlier that the victim was found dead in a rented house in Kampung Katagayan at about 2pm.
Villagers later tracked down and apprehended the suspect at a farm hut in Kampung Sukung before handing him over to police.
f45cc3099933919c: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Football League (MFL) has defended its scheduling of Selangor's fixtures, saying the Red Giants received the minimum two-day rest and travel period between matches.

The clarification followed criticism from Selangor coach Kim Pan Gon over the tight turnaround, after his team beat Sabah 2-1 on Wednesday to reach the FA Cup quarter-finals 4-3 on aggregate at the MBPJ Stadium.
Selangor defeated Melaka 3-2 in the Super League at 8.15pm on Sunday before kicking off against Sabah at 9pm on Wednesday, leaving 48 hours and 45 minutes between matches.
Pan Gon said the schedule contributed to player fatigue, which led to Sabah's equaliser, and called for better protection for players.
"Which team play after about 48 hours? We need everybody to be fair, give proper rest, and protect players," said Pan Gon.
MFL said its schedule ensures a minimum two-day rest and travel window for all 12 M-League clubs this season.
It added that clubs also receive rest periods exceeding two days at various points in the season, in line with previous campaigns.
MFL said club chief executive officers and representatives were notified of the scheduling policy during a meeting on Aug 14 and via a circular on July 21.
The league organiser said adjustments were made following schedule confirmations for the Asean Club Championship, AFC Champions League Elite, AFC Champions League Two, and the FA Cup.
Further changes were required due to recent haze, venue restrictions from government events, and stadium upgrading works.
"We understand the concerns of club coaches regarding player fitness and match quality, and always take player welfare into consideration," said MFL.

"However, the competition calendar also has to take into account the FIFA 2026-27 calendar, 2026 AFF Cup, ACLE, ACL2 and ACC, as well as VAR logistics and operations, club travel requirements and federal and state public holidays."

928d324e2112fd79: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump suggested he might be willing to allow a Chinese car company to build electric vehicles in the US if it did so with American workers, while pledging to maintain the effective US ban on imported vehicles from China.

Trump, speaking in a Fox News interview, rejected the suggestion that he would allow Chinese cars to be imported into the US. “We don’t allow his cars into the United States, and we never did,” Trump said, referring to Chinese leader Xi Jinping, adding that if that wasn’t the case the US automobile market would be “overrun”.

“Now, if China wanted to come in, and open a plant to build their cars here, I’d be okay with it -- Japan does it -- but they hire our people,” Trump said. “The big thing is they hire our people, they use our people.”
“What I don’t want is them to build in Mexico and just, you know, build it inexpensively and ship it across the border,” he said. “That’s un-happening.”

Cheap, tech-laden Chinese EVs from companies like BYD and Geely are rapidly gaining global market share. They’re also appearing in both Canada and Mexico, amplifying concerns among US auto executives that they could soon seek inroads in America.

Currently, Chinese vehicles are essentially shut out of the US market by steep tariffs and a commerce department ban on national security grounds that covers so-called connected vehicle systems from US adversaries including China.
Trump’s comments come weeks before a planned summit with Xi in Washington, though he has made similar remarks before.

In a January speech at the Detroit Economic Club, in the heartland of the American motor vehicle industry, Trump indicated he would be open to allowing Chinese automakers to build cars in the US, saying “let China come in”.

Ford CEO Jim Farley and Trump cabinet members earlier this year held a preliminary informal discussion about how a potential framework might work in which Chinese automakers could build cars in America while offering some protection for domestic companies. No decisions were made at the time on the matter, according to people familiar with the discussions.

Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin, a Democrat whose state includes the headquarters of Ford Motor Co in Dearborn and General Motors Co in Detroit, warned earlier this week against letting Chinese cars enter the US marketplace at all.

“We hear rumors that Trump is planning to allow Chinese cars to be sold in the US, as part of a larger deal he’s putting together,” Slotkin said, adding that to do so would be a “strategic mistake” that would “irrevocably impact” not only the American auto industry but the overall manufacturing capacity of the US, risking jobs.
Trump told Fox News the suggestion that he would allow Chinese cars to be imported into the US was a “total phony rumor”, adding he’s the “only one stopping them”.

Slotkin and Bernie Moreno, an Ohio Republican senator who owned auto dealerships around Cleveland before entering politics, introduced legislation that would ban connected vehicles, software and hardware linked to adversarial countries including China.

The broadly written measure, backed by Ford, GM and the United Auto Workers, would prohibit the sale of connected vehicles by automakers that are more than 15% owned by Chinese entities. However, the legislation as originally drafted has raised concerns that it may inadvertently bar other foreign automakers like Mercedes-Benz Group AG, which has nearly 20% Chinese ownership.
c8b0fa793a849649: PETALING JAYA: Umno will also be conceding failure if it criticises Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's leadership as weak, since the party is part of the government, says Amanah secretary-general Faiz Fadzil.

Faiz said Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's remark that his party was "capable of doing better", made during his policy speech at the Umno general assembly yesterday, only highlighted Zahid's own failure to support the administration.
"If he wants to say the Anwar government has failed, that means he too has failed to help. He too has failed as part of the government," he told FMT.
Faiz said the performance of Anwar's administration should be assessed collectively, since the government was formed through a coalition involving several parties, including Umno.

He also said that data on foreign direct investment (FDI), the ringgit's performance, economic growth, and the Corruption Perceptions Index showed the Anwar government's achievements were better than those of previous administrations.
"You can say whatever you want, but data doesn't lie," he said, adding that the public could make their own assessment based on the government's track record.
Faiz also cited an example under the Anwar-led government, which successfully paid out all outstanding goods and services tax (GST) refunds totalling RM19 billion.
He said the GST, introduced under the previous Barisan Nasional government, had driven up prices, while Pakatan Harapan had since reduced prices and cleared the RM19 billion in claims.
"So how can we say the previous government's policies were better than now?" he asked.

He also cautioned Umno against issuing statements that could destabilise the government, if the party was genuinely committed to maintaining political stability until the end of the current term, as its leadership has claimed.
On broader political developments, Faiz said PH needed to prepare for the possibility that BN may not cooperate with it in the next general election.

"The results of the two state elections (in Johor and Negeri Sembilan) should serve as a wake-up call for PH to strengthen its own machinery and not depend on cooperation with other parties," he said.
In his policy speech at the Umno general assembly, Zahid, who is also the deputy prime minister, referred to unnamed parties as "enough is enough", and to "give us a chance too".
cc3bde5d732f3611: KUALA LUMPUR: The Prisons Department has denied claims of double standards in the release of former Sabah infrastructure minister Datuk Peter Anthony under the Licensed Prisoner Release Programme (PBSL).
The department said he remained under supervision while serving the remainder of his sentence in the community.

"He was considered for PBSL only after reaching the stipulated eligibility period and undergoing the same screening and assessment process applied to other prisoners considered for the programme," the department said in a statement.
It said his release under the programme did not mean the remainder of his court-imposed sentence had been waived.
"Instead, he continues to serve the remainder of his sentence in the community and remains subject to the stipulated conditions, regulations and monitoring throughout the period.

"PBSL was implemented for eligible prisoners regardless of their background, position, status or influence," it said, adding that a person's status was not a criterion that provided any advantage or exemption from the programme's eligibility and assessment process.
"Therefore, claims that release through PBSL is granted based on different treatment or double standards are inaccurate.
"Every consideration is based on the stipulated eligibility, assessment and processes, while prisoners granted PBSL remain under supervision until they complete the remainder of their sentence."
The department said PBSL is a structured community rehabilitation mechanism for prisoners who meet the stipulated requirements and eligibility criteria.
It said the programme does not erase, shorten or reduce a sentence imposed by the courts.
"Those released under the programme continue serving the remainder of their sentences in the community, subject to conditions, regulations, supervision and monitoring by the department.
"To be considered for PBSL, a prisoner must have served at least one-third of the sentence. However, reaching that threshold does not automatically qualify a prisoner for the programme," it said.

The department added that candidates must undergo screening and assessment covering factors including their character and conduct while serving their sentence, rehabilitation progress, participation in the Human Development Programme, readiness to return to the community, family support, suitability of placement, employment opportunities and post-release monitoring requirements.

"PBSL applications are subsequently considered at Prisons Department headquarters by a committee chaired by the Prisons Commissioner-General and comprising senior officers and representatives of relevant agencies," it said.
The department said the process ensures each case is considered based on eligibility and assessment results in accordance with its established procedures.
The issue resurfaced this week amid the debate over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon bid.
Pakatan Harapan had taken the position that those convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, should serve the full sentences imposed by the courts.

MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong then accused PH of applying a double standard, questioning why there had been no similar uproar when Peter was allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence outside prison.
In March, former Sabah infrastructure minister Datuk Peter Anthony was released on parole after serving part of a three-year jail sentence for a forgery conviction.

f01499780f8e1aa3: JOHOR BARU: Negri Sembilan coach Daniel Gimenez admitted his side were no match for Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) after their 3-0 Super League defeat at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium here on Friday.
Gimenez said JDT players have Asian competition experience, while his squad only played domestically.

"I told my players that JDT were an Asian Champions League Elite-level team, while we were just a Super League team.
"Despite knowing this, we were not afraid of JDT, but the Southern Tigers were simply superior.

f5703b5f9fad0732: GUA MUSANG: Lipstick and face powder may have replaced charcoal and limestone paste in the beauty routines of the Orang Asli from the Temiar tribe, but modernisation has not erased the centuries-old tradition of facial adornment passed down through generations.

Endah Angah, 37, said the practice of painting geometric motifs, including long and wavy lines and dots, on the face remained deeply cherished by her community as an enduring symbol of its cultural heritage.

She said the growing difficulty of sourcing traditional beauty ingredients such as kesumba seeds had led her community to increasingly rely on modern cosmetics, which were easier to obtain than having to venture into the forest in search of the natural materials.
"In the past, these natural ingredients were easy to find, so we didn't have to go deep into the forest to look for them. But now, they're getting harder to find.

"Using modern cosmetics is much easier for us. The red and black colours from lipstick and eyeliner also make the patterns on our faces look neater and brighter, and they last longer too," the housewife told Bernama recently.
Rahimah Punai, 39, said modern cosmetics might have changed the way the facial motifs were created, but their spiritual meaning and connection to their ancestral heritage remained intact.

"We make sure every horizontal and wavy line, as well as every dot, is drawn carefully because each one has its own meaning. The lines represent the river, while the dots symbolise our connection to nature.
"Nothing has changed, except that we now use modern cosmetics. We have to follow what our ancestors passed down to us and keep it the same to preserve our customs and heritage.
"So, we cannot just add streaks to the forehead, nose or cheeks," she said.
Abong Busu, 55, said the custom remained deeply rooted among the Temiar tribe and continued to be practised during religious ceremonies such as the sewang and at community gatherings.
"This is how we introduce the tradition to the younger generation. The children are very interested and often ask us a lot of questions about it," she said.

Meanwhile, Kelantan State Department for Culture and Arts director Rohaniza Abdullah said the use of modern cosmetics, while retaining the original facial motifs, represented a new way of preserving and continuing the traditional heritage practice.

She said creativity in producing modern-style facial decorations was a way to keep the heritage relevant while preserving its originality and aesthetic value as an important part of Orang Asli identity and socio-cultural life.
"The use of modern cosmetics is a positive development for the community because the traditional facial motifs can still be recreated while retaining their original patterns and colours.
"This also helps preserve the tradition for future generations.
"Preserving this tradition for the next generation is important, so efforts by various parties, especially to engage young people, must continue," she said.
She said the uniqueness and symbolism behind the facial motifs could make the traditional art an iconic representation of Orang Asli culture.
5fc0accc0f7b3c11: PETALING JAYA: Pesuruhjaya Kanak-kanak Suruhanjaya Hak Asasi Manusia (Suhakam) menggesa pihak berkuasa tempatan mengenal pasti "hotspot" anjing berkeliaran yang kerap menjadi tumpuan kanak-kanak bagi mencegah serangan terhadap golongan itu.

Katanya, kawasan panas terbabit termasuk sekolah, taska dan tadika, taman permainan, projek perumahan rakyat dan kawasan perumahan pangsapuri, laluan berjalan kaki dan berbasikal ke sekolah, perhentian bas serta lokasi sering menerima aduan anjing liar atau agresif.
Mereka turut menggesa Kementerian Perumahan dan Kerajaan Tempatan, kerajaan negeri dan Jabatan Perkhidmatan Veterinar menetapkan piawaian tindak balas lebih jelas serta berasaskan risiko.

Ia termasuk mengutamakan aduan kumpulan anjing atau anjing agresif di sekitar rumah, sekolah serta taman permainan, menetapkan prosedur operasi standard dan mekanisme tindakan susulan jelas serta memperkukuh pengumpulan data nasional mengenai serangan haiwan membabitkan kanak-kanak.

Kenyataan ini menyusul kes seorang kanak-kanak perempuan dua tahun cedera parah di bahagian kepala dan muka selepas didakwa diserang lima ekor anjing liar berhampiran rumah neneknya di Sungai Kelambu, Johor pada 5 Sept lalu.
Pesuruhjaya Kanak-kanak berkata, kejadian itu tidak patut dianggap kes terpencil kerana terdapat beberapa laporan kanak-kanak diserang atau digigit anjing berkeliaran atau liar sejak 2023.
Mereka turut merujuk kes seorang kanak-kanak lelaki hampir dilanggar kereta ketika dikejar seekor anjing di Sitiawan pada 2024.

"Kanak-kanak mempunyai hak untuk hidup, bermain, berjalan dan pergi ke sekolah dalam persekitaran selamat daripada risiko boleh dijangka dan dicegah," katanya sambil menambah kanak-kanak kecil amat terdedah disebabkan saiz fizikal dan keupayaan terhad untuk mempertahankan diri.

Mereke menegaskan kepentingan pendidikan keselamatan kepada kanak-kanak, ibu bapa, pihak sekolah dan pengendali pusat penjagaan kanak-kanak, termasuk panduan cara mengelakkan haiwan agresif dan mendapatkan rawatan perubatan segera selepas digigit.
Tetapi, katanya, pendidikan keselamatan sama sekali tidak boleh mengalihkan tanggungjawab mengurus risiko keselamatan awam yang diketahui daripada pihak berkuasa kepada kanak-kanak.
"Kanak-kanak kecil tidak seharusnya terpaksa mengelak daripada bermain di luar rumah, taman permainan atau ke sekolah hanya kerana wujud risiko boleh dijangka akibat anjing berkeliaran.
"Apabila bahaya kepada kanak-kanak diketahui dan boleh dicegah, kita tidak boleh menunggu sehingga berlaku satu lagi tragedi sebelum bertindak.

"Pengurusan anjing liar dan agresif yang berkesan bukan semata-mata isu pengurusan haiwan, apabila kanak-kanak terdedah kepada risiko boleh dijangka, ia merupakan isu keselamatan dan perlindungan kanak-kanak."
Mereka berkata, penguatkuasaan perlu berperikemanusiaan dan mematuhi Akta Kebajikan Haiwan 2015 kerana perlindungan kanak-kanak serta kebajikan haiwan "boleh dan mesti dilaksanakan serentak".
786b359592441978: DUBLIN: Donald Trump lands in Ireland under tight security Saturday for two days of diplomacy and golf, on a trip that again blurs the lines between his presidency and personal business interests.
At least 4,000 police and other personnel, including snipers, have been mobilised for the visit, in what has been dubbed one of the biggest security operations ever mounted in Ireland.
Trump spoke briefly to reporters on the tarmac ahead of his flight to Dublin saying "we're having a lot of meetings with European leaders and others, so it'll be very interesting time".

Thousands of anti-Trump protesters are planning to rally in Dublin, where the US leader will hold separate meetings with Ireland's taoiseach (prime minister) Micheal Martin and president Catherine Connolly.
Trump is then due to fly to his luxury resort in Doonbeg, on Ireland's west coast, where some of the world's top golfers are competing in the Irish Open tournament.

The golf-mad president -- whose relaxed relationship with the game's rules was documented by sports journalist Rick Reilly in the 2019 book "Commander in Cheat" -- may even award the trophy on Sunday.
"He's really just visiting the golf resort he owns and dropping into Dublin for a courtesy visit," Daniel Geary, a US history professor at Trinity College Dublin, told AFP.
"He sees little difference between his private interests and his role as president."
'Business'
The 80-year-old billionaire has promoted his family's golf business unabashedly since returning to the White House for his second stint as president in January 2025.
Last summer, he welcomed then-UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and EUchief Ursula von der Leyen to his plush resort at Turnberry on the west coast of Scotland.
Trump then inaugurated another golf course bearing his name in the town of Balmedie, near Aberdeen on the northeast Scottish coast.
"He certainly sends a message that he is passionately interested in his own family's business," University of Minnesota law professor Richard Painter said ahead of the Ireland trip.

"It's not going to help the Republican party in the midterms to have the president... promoting his golf courses for the super-wealthy, when other people are having trouble making ends meet," the expert on government ethics added.

The security operation for Trump's visit is reportedly costing Ireland 20 million euros (US$23 million) and comes as the country already grapples with a massive policing operation for its six-month presidency of the EU.
Trump's attendance at Doonbeg -- a remote, coastal site in County Clare that the Trump Organization purchased in 2014 -- adds an extra layer of complexity to the security effort.
Some 40,000 fans are expected at the tournament over the weekend, with six-time major winner and current world number two Rory McIlroy the main draw.
McIlroy, who has played golf with Trump, told the BBC this week that the tournament will feel "different" with the US president on site, but that the players will just "keep our heads down and play".
'Short and courteous'
After arriving in Dublin on Air Force One, Trump will meet Irish leader Martin, whom he has hosted twice in the Oval Office and appears to get on well with.
The Middle East, including America's and Israel's war on Iran, and US tariffs on EU pharmaceuticals and immigration are likely to be on the agenda.
Ireland and the US have long been close allies, partly because of their common ancestral ties.
But the Irish government's politics diverge sharply with that of the Trump administration on many issues -- particularly support for the Palestinians.
Ireland is among several countries, including Spain, the UK and France, that have announced a trade ban targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
Connolly, who occupies the largely ceremonial role of president, is a left-winger and outspoken critic of Trump, making for a potentially fractious first meeting.
"Martin is experienced enough that it should be fine at the political level. The big uncertainty is President Connolly," Eoin O'Malley, a political scientist at Dublin City University, told AFP.

"She protested against his last visit (in 2019), and her supporters will expect her to make some show for them. But she's also aware that she cannot do or say anything that might inflict damage on the relationship.
"I expect it will be short and courteous."
392c7dbd6ad1e778: MADRID, Sept 12 — Max Verstappen did not mince his words on Friday after finishing sixth in second practice, four-tenths adrift of pace-setting championship leader Kimi Antonelli, at the Spanish Grand Prix.
Asked how he liked his first day’s running on the new high-risk hybrid Madring circuit on the outskirts of Madrid, he said: “I’m not a fan of street circuits.”
“That will never change. And I will always prefer to drive on a track like Spa (in Belgium).
“But what they have done in the way they have built everything up, I think they’ve done a really good job. But I am not a fan of street circuits.”
Verstappen said he was not surprised at his performance or position after two hours on the track he had described as “challenging” and said he had finished as expected.

“From our side, it’s more or less where we are. We just need to work a little bit more on the balance and try to get more out one lap and then see how the tyres hold up on the long run, but I guess everyone is in the same boat.”

His Red Bull team-mate, Liam Lawson, substituting for the injured Isack Hadjar, was 10th as Mercedes and Ferrari set the pace throughout a day of unexpectedly straightforward action with only one red flag.
That came when Racing Bulls’ impressive rookie Arvid Lindblad crashed in second practice. Most paddock observers including drivers had forecast a series of accidents and red flags.
Lindblad ended the day fourth fastest behind Antonelli, Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton with George Russell fifth in the second Mercedes.
Verstappen was sixth ahead of McLaren’s Oscar Piastri whose team-mate Lando Norris managed only two laps before pitting for a new gearbox in the second session.
“That’s a big setback for him,” said McLaren technical director Mark Temple. “Going into FP3, we’ll be trying to do as much as we can to give him back track time.” — AFP
1338d56428ced3e7: LONDON, Sept 12 — Captain Jared Bowen scored the opener as West Ham surged back to the top of the Championship table with a 6-0 thrashing of Wrexham on Friday.

The Hammers had lost top spot to West Brom on Wednesday after the Baggies claimed a narrow 1-0 win at Derby, thanks to Aune Heggebo and despite playing for more than an hour with 10 men following Brayann Pereira’s dismissal.
Bowen opened the scoring on 28 minutes when he touched home Morato’s low cross for his sixth goal of the season.
Argentina international Taty Castellanos selflessly teed up Dutch-born Suriname forward Joel Piroe to double West Ham’s lead on 37 minutes.
And the contest was all-but-over three minutes after the restart as Greece centre-back Konstantinos Mavropanos headed home Bowen’s corner.
Castellanos was next to get in on the act as he scored from a pass by Kyle Walker-Peters.
Manor Solomon played in substitute Mohamadou Kante for the fifth and scored the sixth himself from Walker-Peters’s square pass.
West Brom could regain top spot with victory at home to fourth-placed QPR on Saturday.
QPR, Charlton and Swansea could all mathematically overtake West Hame but they would need to win by unlikely scorelines to do so. — AFP
78262f42737e151b: ROME, Sept 12 — Argentinian teenager Franco Mastantuono scored a hat-trick on Friday as Fiorentina earned their first points of the Serie A season with a 4-2 win at fellow strugglers Venezia.
Fiorentina, who had been winless and last in Serie A, rehired Paolo Vanoli on Monday to replace Fabio Grosso, who was sacked after losing his first three matches.
And in a clash between two sides who had yet to register a point this season, Nigerian Akor Adams got hosts Venezia off the mark after 22 minutes.
But 19-year-old Mastantuono, who is on loan from Real Madrid, scored twice within a minute on the half-hour mark for his first Serie A goals.
Mateo Pellegrino came off the bench after an hour and found the net six minutes later before Mastantuono completed his hat-trick after 84 minutes.
French midfielder Antoine Hainaut pulled a second back for Venezia with four minutes to go.
Fiorentina moved up to 15th as Venezia dropped to last place, with both clubs having conceded 11 goals in their first four matches. — AFP
99d2a16e8261cb41: PETALING JAYA: A veiled social media exchange between Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and his deputy, Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, continued today, with the Umno president appearing to respond to the prime minister's post last night from New Delhi, India.
In a Facebook post today, Zahid thanked his followers for tuning in to his policy speech at the Umno general assembly yesterday, “whether you were in the country or abroad”.
"God willing, I will deliver the closing address this afternoon. Continue to follow me, wherever you are," he said.
Zahid’s post came hours after Anwar, who arrived in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, referred to himself as a “guru” in a Facebook post.

Anwar said he hoped his “students” would learn how “Madani Diplomacy” was translated into practice, signing off the post with “Slayyy” and a nail-polish emoji with a yellow hand and pink manicured nails.
The Gen Z-language-filled post appeared to reference Zahid’s use of the word “guru” in a remark criticising the government’s handling of the Budi95 petrol subsidy programme.

Zahid had said the subsidised fuel quota was cut from 300 litres to 200 litres a month in April before being restored to 300 litres on Sept 1, arguing that such reversals had caused confusion among the public.
"Cukup, cukuplah, guru. Listen to our voices, guru. We can do better than what the guru has done," he said.
In the same speech, Zahid had also showed off his knowledge of Gen Z lingo, urging Umno’s younger members to “slay” and “flex”.
Zahid’s remarks came after he denied last Sunday that his relationship with Anwar had become increasingly strained.
This followed a Bloomberg report that tensions between the two leaders were worsening, with recent Cabinet meetings taking place for shorter periods than usual.

Bloomberg reported that the tensions stemmed from Zahid’s decision for Barisan Nasional to contest against Pakatan Harapan in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, as well as DAP’s pressure for institutional reforms.
19b5637abd294760: NEW YORK: Big-serving Ben Shelton overpowered American compatriot Frances Tiafoe in four sets to reach the first Grand Slam final of his career at the US Open on Friday.

Eighth-seeded Shelton blasted 20 aces on his way to a thrilling 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 victory on the Arthur Ashe Stadium court that sends the 23-year-old into Sunday's championship match against top-seeded Alexander Zverev of Germany.
A pulsating all-American semi-final had seen both players vying to reach a Grand Slam final for the first time.

Shelton -- who took down defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals -- will now have the chance to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam title since 2003, when Andy Roddick triumphed at the US Open.
Tiafoe got off to a bright start, claiming the first set after breaking when Shelton uncharacteristically double-faulted to trail at 5-4.
Tiafoe held to love to clinch the first set but Shelton came flying out of the blocks to start the second.
An early break helped him into a 2-0 lead before Tiafoe responded with a break to level at 2-2.
Yet with Tiafoe's serve increasingly erratic, Shelton grabbed another break in the eighth game to go 5-3 up and then held to level.
The momentum was all with Shelton and Tiafoe had to fight off two break points before holding early in the third set.
However Shelton – who had one serve initially clocked at 158mph before it was later adjusted to 144mph -- made no mistake in the fifth game with a break to go 3-2 up.
Tiafoe needed to hold to keep the set alive in the ninth game, and a furious arm-wrestle saw the 11th seed once again save three break and set points.
Shelton though earned his fourth break point after pouncing on Tiafoe's second serve once more, scorching a backhand return down the line.
Shelton converted that when Tiafoe netted a forehand to find himself 2-1 down.
The fourth set went with serve until the 12th game, when Shelton grabbed the crucial break to seal victory.

8fe831018b66fa2c: MIRI: The DNA test results for the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang in Baram have been obtained, and the remains will be handed over to the next of kin today, says Sarawak police commissioner Zainal Abdullah.
“Today, once the documentation is completed, the remains will be handed over to the families,” he told Bernama when contacted.
Meanwhile, funeral arrangements are under way for three of the five victims, as their families prepare to bid their final farewells.
Medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry will be laid to rest at the Anglican Cemetery in Lambir following a funeral service at the Good Shepherd Church in Lutong at 9am on Sept 15.
His sister, Annastasia Luyah, said in a funeral notice shared on her Facebook last night that a wake will be held on Sept 14 at their family residence at Taman Desa Senadin here.

The wake for staff nurse Jessie Paya Jok will be held at Taman Wang Lusut while the body of staff nurse Debra Moset will be brought home to Kampung Semadang in Padawan, Kuching, for a wake service. The burial dates have yet to be announced.
All five people on board the BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace were killed after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at about 3.40pm on Sept 8.
The other two who lost their lives were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin and pilot Zainol Afiq Bee Sham.
Ainul is expected to be laid to rest at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery in Kelantan, while Zainol will be brought home to Negeri Sembilan for burial.

Yesterday, Zainal said post-mortem examinations on all five victims were completed at the forensic department of Miri Hospital on Thursday night and the DNA analysis was expected to be completed today.
aaaa0c51101d0b85: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — A section of Jalan Syed Putra and Jalan Istana intersection here will be closed in stages starting September 14, from 10pm to 5am, to facilitate preliminary construction work for the New Pantai Expressway Extension Project (NPE 2).

1cee3a1a00fa8afa: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The ringgit is expected to trade within a tight range against the US dollar next week, with investors remaining cautious ahead of key monetary policy decisions by the United States Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Japan (BOJ).

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the focus next week will be on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) and BOJ monetary policy meetings. Both central banks are expected to raise their respective policy rates by 25 basis points.

Market participants will also monitor the Fed’s latest economic projections closely for gross domestic product (GDP) growth, inflation, the unemployment rate and the federal funds rate, he told Bernama.
“Expectations of a rate hike by the US Fed have shaped sentiment in the foreign exchange market, lending support to the US dollar,” he said.
Against this backdrop, Mohd Afzanizam said the ringgit is likely to remain within a tight range of between RM4.06 and RM4.08 against the US dollar next week.
He also said external developments, particularly the sharp rise in crude oil prices amid the intensifying US-Israel-Iran conflict, are also expected to influence market sentiment.
“The escalation has pushed Brent crude oil prices higher to around US$104.64 (RM425.91) per barrel,” he said.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit weakened against the greenback to 4.0685/0725 from 4.0425/0465 a week earlier.
The local currency traded lower against a basket of major currencies during the week.

The ringgit depreciated against the British pound to 5.4961/5015 from 5.4663/4717 last Friday, fell against the Japanese yen to 2.6400/6428 from 2.5832/5860, and declined against the euro to 4.7178/7225 from 4.6962/7008.
It also traded lower against Asean currencies.
The local note weakened against the Singapore dollar to 3.2091/2125 from 3.1888/1923 a week earlier and depreciated against the Thai baht to 12.3072/3241 from 12.2693/2863.
It also declined against the Indonesian rupiah to 231.0/231.3 from 229.1/229.4 and eased against the Philippine peso to 6.49/6.50 from 6.45/6.46 last Friday. — Bernama
fd135bf47976820e: LOS ANGELES: Pop superstar Lady Gaga welcomed her first child with fiance Michael Polansky, US media reported Friday.
The 40-year-old "Bad Romance" singer, whose real name is Stefani Germanotta, began dating Polansky in 2020, and became engaged to the entrepreneur in 2024.
A source confirmed news of the child's birth to Page Six and People, but no additional details about the baby, including its name, sex or date of birth, were immediately available.

1d2a8cb08aafce81: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Bursa Malaysia could see selective bargain hunting next week following the recent sell-off, particularly in fundamentally sound blue-chip stocks that have been marked down amid the broader risk-off environment, an analyst said.

Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said external developments are likely to remain the key driver of sentiment, with movements in crude oil prices and United States (US) Treasury yields closely watched.
“We expect the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) to consolidate at current levels with scope for a technical recovery should global risk sentiment stabilise.
“We anticipate the benchmark index to trend within the range of 1,680-1,710 for next week,” he told Bernama.

He said investors would closely monitor the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision next week, with markets increasingly pricing in a 25 basis point rate hike amid elevated oil prices and renewed inflationary pressures.
“A rate hike would mark the first increase since July 2023 and could weigh further on global risk appetite and emerging-market equities.
“Technically, the local bourse has formed a bearish candlestick to dip below the 1,700 psychological level,” he said.
Hence, Leong said the next supports are now located at 1,680 points and 1,676 points, while the immediate resistances are shifted to 1,714 points, followed by 1,722 points.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) declined 21.36 points to 1,686.74 at yesterday’s close from 1,708.10 a week earlier.

By sector, the Energy Index advanced 8.81 points to 814.43, and the Plantation Index improved 98.10 points to 9,436.02, while the Industrial Products and Services Index rose 1.82 points to 188.78, and the Financial Services Index dipped 539.28 points to 19,622.21.
Weekly turnover increased to 18.97 billion units worth RM15.53 billion from 17.97 billion units worth RM14.14 billion in the prior week.
Main Market volume eased to 11.62 billion units valued at RM13.89 billion against 12.00 billion units valued at RM12.85 billion previously.
Warrants turnover expanded to 4.40 billion units worth RM624.83 million versus 3.83 billion units worth RM542.71 million last week.
ACE Market volume strengthened to 2.93 billion units valued at RM1.00 million compared with 2.13 billion units valued at RM743.53 million in the previous week. — Bernama
74cab536eec3aef0: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) expects another three international airlines to commence flights to Kuala Lumpur by the end of this year, further strengthening the city’s connectivity as a regional aviation hub.
Its managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said the development would be in addition to German-based Lufthansa Airlines’ planned return to Kuala Lumpur this October.

“In terms of connectivity, we have many new airlines coming (to Kuala Lumpur) this year. For example, Lufthansa Airlines is coming to Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 in October, so we are excited about it.

“(Including Lufthansa), we are expecting four (international) airlines from now until the end of the year. We will announce (the details of the airlines) soon,” he told Bernama at the sidelines of MAHB Official Visit to Wisma Bernama on Friday.
Mohd Izani and MAHB management were received by Bernama Chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai, Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, and Editor-in-Chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj.
The delegation was also received by Deputy Editor-in-Chief (News Service) Mohd Shukri Ishak, Deputy Editor-in-Chief (Economic News Service) Harlina Samson, and other senior officials.
The official visit provided a good opportunity for the MAHB team to come together with Bernama, exchange ideas and explore areas of collaboration, he said.

Meanwhile, Mohd Izani said MAHB remained mindful of external factors, including uncertain weather conditions and geopolitical developments, which could impact its operations, while prioritising the continuity of air connectivity.
“We are mindful of the (uncertain weather conditions) situation. Again, our objective is to make sure that connectivity continues.

“We continue to promote Malaysia. As you know, the crisis in West Asia did have some impact, but based on our numbers in July, (air traffic) has improved, and hopefully in the coming months until the end of the year, we will continue to improve,” he said.

He also welcomed the government’s announcement that 2027 would also be designated as a Visit Malaysia Year, saying the initiative would benefit both KLIA and the country by strengthening the airport’s role as a gateway for international visitors to Malaysia.
On July 22, MAHB recorded 51 million passenger movements across its Malaysian airport network in the first half of financial year 2026, an increase of 1.8 per cent from the same period last year.
It said the positive performance was driven by sustained international travel demand despite weaker domestic traffic. — Bernama
b31d4bfbc92da998: PETALING JAYA: Umno juga sebenarnya gagal jika mengkritik pimpinan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim lemah kerana parti itu sebahagian kerajaan, kata Setiausaha Agung Amanah Faiz Fadzil.

Katanya, apa disebut Presiden Zahid Hamidi yang partinya 'mampu melakukan lebih baik' ketika berucap pada Perhimpunan Agung Umno (PAU) semalam, tidak lebih daripada menunjukkan kegagalannya membantu pentadbiran.

“Kalau dia nak kata kerajaan Anwar ini gagal, maksudnya beliau pun gagal membantu itu. Beliau pun gagal sebagai sebahagian kerajaan,” katanya kepada FMT sambil berkata kejayaan pentadbiran Anwar perlu dilihat secara kolektif kerana kerajaan dibentuk melalui gabungan beberapa parti, termasuk Umno.

Beliau berkata, data berkaitan pelaburan langsung asing, prestasi ringgit, pertumbuhan ekonomi dan indeks persepsi rasuah (CPI) menunjukkan pencapaian kerajaan Anwar lebih baik, berbanding pentadbiran terdahulu.

96dc64a55d1760fd: JAKARTA: A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck near Jakarta’s Thousand Islands early Saturday, with tremors felt in the Indonesian capital and across parts of Java and Sumatra.

Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) Earthquake and Tsunami director Wijayanto said the earthquake struck at 4.23 am local time, with the magnitude revised from an initial 5.9 following further analysis.
He said its epicentre was in the Java Sea, 69km northeast of Jakarta’s Thousand Islands, at a depth of 368km.

“Taking into account the location of the epicentre and the depth of its hypocentre, the earthquake was a deep earthquake caused by intraslab activity,” he said in a statement, adding that tsunami modelling showed no tsunami threat.

The earthquake came less than 10 hours after a magnitude 6.0 quake struck the Banda Sea in eastern Indonesia at 6.56 pm on Friday at a depth of 148km, with its epicentre 162km northeast of Southwest Maluku and tremors felt across parts of Maluku.

Wijayanto said the strongest tremors from Saturday’s earthquake were reported in parts of Banten and West Java, as well as Tanggamus in southern Sumatra, where the shaking was perceptible by people indoors and could cause windows and doors to rattle.

He said the tremors were also clearly felt indoors in Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok and several other areas, while weaker shaking was reported as far away as Yogyakarta and Malang in Java, and Padang and the Mentawai Islands in western Sumatra.

Some of strongest tremors were reportedly felt in Pandeglang in Banten, which lies along the Sunda Strait near the Anak Krakatau volcano which experienced renewed eruptive activity last week. However, Wijayanto said, Saturday’s earthquake was tectonic in origin, with BMKG reporting no aftershocks as of 5 am.
Meanwhile, KAI Commuter said in a social media post that Commuter Line services were suspended following the earthquake to allow comprehensive inspections of railway tracks.
It said the Bogor, Cikarang, Rangkasbitung, and Tanjung Priok lines resumed services after inspections were completed at 5.26 am , followed by the Tangerang line at 5.45 am.

cf64df85e967ed6d: PETALING JAYA: Local authorities should map “child-sensitive roaming-dog hotspots” to prevent attacks on children, say the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia’s (Suhakam) children’s commissioners.

The commissioners said the hotspots should include schools, kindergartens, playgrounds, PPR and flats housing areas, school routes, and locations with repeated complaints about roaming or aggressive dogs.

In a statement, they also called for the housing and local government ministry, state governments, local authorities, and the veterinary services department (DVS) to adopt clearer, risk-based measures to manage the problem.

These should include prioritising complaints involving packs of aggressive dogs near homes and schools, establishing standard procedures for escalation and follow-up, and improving national data on animal attacks involving children.
The call follows an attack on a two-year-old girl who was allegedly attacked by five stray dogs near her grandmother’s house in Sungai Kelambu, Johor, on the morning of Sept 5.
The girl suffered serious injuries to her head and face and was taken to a district hospital before being transferred to Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Bahru.
The children's commissioners said the incident should not be treated as an isolated case, citing several reports of children being attacked or bitten by roaming or stray dogs since 2023.
They also pointed to cases where children were hurt while fleeing dogs. In Sitiawan in 2024, a boy ran into traffic while being chased by a dog and was nearly hit by a car.

"Children have a right to live, play, walk and travel to school in an environment that is reasonably safe from foreseeable and preventable risks," they said, adding that young children are particularly vulnerable because of their size and limited ability to defend themselves.

They stressed that safety education for children, parents, schools and childcare providers was important, including guidance on avoiding aggressive animals and seeking prompt medical attention after a bite.
However, such education should not shift responsibility for managing a known public safety risk from authorities to children.
“A young child should not have to avoid playing outside their home, using a playground or travelling to school because of a foreseeable risk posed by roaming dogs,” the commissioners said.
“When a danger to children is known and reasonably preventable, we cannot wait for another tragedy before acting.”
They said managing roaming and aggressive dogs was not merely an animal-management issue but also a matter of child safety and protection when children were exposed to foreseeable risks.

However, they added that enforcement on stray dogs must remain humane and lawful under the Animal Welfare Act 2015, stressing that child protection and animal welfare “can and must be pursued together”.

5d112465d867597a: KUALA LUMPUR: Asean health ministers concluded their five-day biennial meeting in Kuala Lumpur with a five-year health agenda and steps to strengthen the region’s preparedness for future health emergencies.
The 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting (AHMM), which ended on Friday, saw the official launch of the Asean Strategic Health Agenda (ASHA) 2026-2030 on Wednesday morning.
The agenda covers four areas - promoting healthy lifestyles, responding to health emergencies and emerging threats, strengthening health systems and access to care, and ensuring food safety.

However, launching the agenda is only the first step, as health ministry deputy director for global health Dr Juliana Sharmini Paul said member states will lead different projects according to their respective capacities.

“Malaysia is leading the Asean Emergency Operations Centre, through which we host webinars, bring in experts, and go over to other Asean countries for consultations on infectious diseases and beyond,” she told FMT.
She said most of the projects under ASHA are expected to be completed by 2030, with progress to be regularly reviewed by Asean health officials and ministers.
FMT takes a look at the outcomes of the 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting, how Malaysia fits into the region’s health plans, and what happens next.
ACPHEED not operational yet

Juliana noted that the Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases (ACPHEED), intended to coordinate expertise and regional responses to outbreaks or health emergencies, is not yet operational.
She said member states had moved closer to finalising the agreement to establish the centre. “Once that is finalised, then it can be signed and put into operation,” she said.
ACPHEED is expected to help coordinate access to vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics, while individual countries continue to operate their own surveillance systems.
Malaysia-led priorities
The meeting saw the launch of the Asean Action Plan for Lung Health, with Malaysia sharing its experience in using AI-assisted chest X-ray screening.
Juliana said lung health and tobacco control were high on the priority list for most member states.
Malaysia presented its Rare Diseases Playbook during a side event, with proposals requiring the consensus of all member states before they can become regional priorities.

Juliana said regional programmes could draw on funding from Asean’s dialogue and development partners rather than relying solely on domestic budgets, while collaborations with external organisations require member-state approval.
She said the impact of some initiatives would take time to assess, especially those aimed at improving population health.
“It’s not something you can just measure over one year or even two years. It will take time to see an improvement in the health status of the people at large,” she said.
What Malaysia must do next

Ilyana Mukhriz, a research associate at the Khazanah Research Institute, said the challenge for Malaysia now was to translate the regional commitments made at the meeting into tangible improvements to its health system.
Ilyana said on-the-ground action and appropriate fiscal commitments were necessary to ensure tangible benefits.

Pooled procurement at the Asean level, for example, could improve access to essential medicines and newer treatments while reducing pharmaceutical costs for the government and patients’ out-of-pocket spending.

She said Malaysia and its regional partners should also build local production capacity to reduce their dependence on global supply chains, pointing to the difficulties in accessing supplies during the Covid-19 pandemic.
“In this sense, we as part of Asean need to develop more regional production hubs to become less vulnerable,” she said.

Ilyana said closer cooperation was also needed to protect Malaysia from cross-border disease threats, including through real-time outbreak monitoring, effective data systems, and regional standard operating procedures for rapid responses.

She said progress could be measured through indicators such as drug costs, out-of-pocket spending, availability of critical medicines in public health facilities, and procurement lead times for advanced medical devices under the proposed single-submission model.
“However, the true test of the success of this regional health collaboration may only be visible during cross-border public health emergencies,” she said.

Ilyana said that with Malaysia preparing to hand over the Asean health sector chairmanship, continuity would require codified frameworks, monitoring and evaluation, and public reporting to ensure regional health ministries remain accountable for their commitments.
